“My blessing has benefited me greatly.” Sparks of lighting began to emerge from the old man’s arms. “I am no longer sure exactly how high my lightning affinity is, but I know that it is at least six-star.”
Small balls of lightning appeared in his hands and he tossed them in the air, as if juggling them, showing his adept control of the erratic element. “However, that is only the merest fraction of my blessing. Each time I have ascended a realm, I have been granted a legacy in the art of talisman crafting. I can currently be considered a Peak Rank 3 Talisman Artist.”
After saying this, he demonstrated his abilities with talismans. When he was done, he gave a final bow and planted his feet as he waited to hear how he had been judged.
The woman from the Verdant Forest Sect was the first to speak. “You are indeed skilled, Grandmaster Murong, but my sect cannot provide a proper place for someone with your talents.”
The man from Rising Sun gave a contemptuous smirk. “You may join my empire. We will allow you to craft for us, and if you do a suitable job, we may allow you an opportunity to ascend in due time."
The man from the Flowing Mountain tapped on his armrest and nodded. “The Flowing Mountain Sect will offer you a position. As long as you teach our disciples well, we will grant you a temporary position as an elder that will allow you to advance. Whether you can keep this position will be up to you.”
The man from the Rising Sun looked like he was about to say something, but before he could, I stepped forward from the other side of the arena.
“Grandmaster Murong, I would like to offer you a position within the Su Clan. If you join us, I guarantee that you will be able to ascend to Martial Lord. Your time will be yours to do with as you please. If you wish to teach, you may. If you wish to craft, you may. Nothing will be required of you, but you will receive rewards commensurate with your contributions.”
For a long moment, everyone froze in shock. Then, a voice broke the silence.
“
What!?
” The young man from the Rising Sun glared at me. “How dare you challenge the might of the Rising Sun Empire!?”
I waved a dismissive hand. “I have no interest in challenging anyone. I am simply offering Grandmaster Murong another option. He may choose it or disregard it at his leisure.”
Snarling, the young man turned to one of his guards. “Kill him.”
Immediately, the guard rushed at me.
I smiled and pulled off my outer robe, revealing the Rank 3 refined armor underneath. Then, I reached down and picked up a Rank 3 refined staff.
Seeing this, the three recruiters gawked in horror, but the guard didn’t even pause. He just continued his charge.
With a single, light swing of my staff, I knocked him senseless. Then, I turned to the man at the center of the arena. “Grandmaster Murong, please make your choice. Don’t worry, I won’t compel you to follow me.”
Murong NaYun stared at me. He had said that he had traveled outside the Wastes in his youth, so he likely knew what my weapon and armor represented, at least a bit.
He glanced at the Flowing Mountain recruiter and then back to me. “Are you certain that you can help me advance to Martial Lord?”
I nodded. “I guarantee it.”
Clenching his fists, he stood there in silence for several long minutes as he considered my offer.
Finally, he bowed. “Very well, Grandmaster Su. I will follow you.”
Each of the recruiters looked like they wanted to say something, but I only glared at them before leading Murong NaYun away.
Once we were out of sight, I pulled Grandmaster Murong into my inner world and sent him to have a talk with a couple of my Revered Elders. Then, I circled back to watch the rest of the day’s events.
After we disappeared, the host and the recruiters did their best to return a sense of normalcy to the proceedings, but an underlying tension remained.
Several more hopefuls stepped forward to show off their skills, but only one ended up being recruited. That lucky person was a middle-aged man who was dressed like a hobo and looked like he hadn’t bathed in weeks. However, I was likely the only person who knew this since he was covered in a thick layer of light and dark qi, making him invisible.
When the Rising Sun’s recruiter saw this person, he chuckled evilly and glanced at where I attacked his guard. Then, he immediately offered the man a position in his retinue.
After that, the day’s festivities came to an end.
I spent that night in a house on the outskirts of the Su Clan’s palace complex.
The next morning, the Grandmasters’ martial arts tournament began. With a full day having passed, the tense atmosphere created by me recruiting Grandmaster Murong had dissipated, and people were able to enjoy the fighting. When the recruiters saw the prizes on offer, though, they turned green with envy.
Perfect Rank 3 pills, Profound- and Earth-Rank combat techniques, and high-quality Rank 3 refined weapons. Even in their powerful factions, only the best of the best would have been given access to such items.
In a usual year, only two or three of the competitors might have had a shot at being recruited. This time, however, every single person who placed in the top 10—everyone who had received a prize—was offered a position in the Rising Sun Empire. A couple of them were smart enough to reject this offer, but most of them took it, even knowing that it would mean forfeiting their winnings.
That night, I returned to my lonely house on the outskirts of the Su Clan’s complex and sat down in the middle of my room to cultivate.
After hours of waiting there, I was starting to worry that my guess had been incorrect. However, shortly after midnight, I was knocked to the ground by a hard kick to my chest.
Two long steel rods impaled me on either side of my body and pinned me to the floor.
I turned on energy vision and scanned my surroundings, but I didn’t see anything.
“Interesting…”
Something slapped my face, and an ominous voice echoed out around me. “Where did the Su Clan get access to so many high-quality items?”
When I didn’t respond immediately, something kicked me in the ribs. “Answer, now. Otherwise, I will kill you.”Thɪs updatᴇd by NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
Silently, I flicked my hand and sent out a wisp of qi to activate the room's formations.
“What? What have you done!?”
Ignoring the voice, I mentally tugged on the two rods impaling me and sent them into my inner world. Then, I looked at the corner of the room. Using energy vision, I stared and tried to make out any details that I could. However, no matter how hard I tried, I saw nothing.
“Interesting. Your blessing gives you absolute invisibility? During the competition, were you just using light and dark qi to mask your true capabilities? What are your limitations? They must exist, right?”
“What… What do you want?” The voice was frantic, and I could sense that this person was trying to free himself—not that it mattered. He had no chance of escaping from my Rank 5 formation.
I smiled at the empty air in front of me. “You should know, there were formations in place to stop you from killing me. You never had a chance. Your employer sent you here to die.”
“What…”
I shook my head sorrowfully. “Be more honest in your next life and don’t offend those you can’t afford to offend.”
Pulling out a sword, I slashed at the empty air.
Suddenly, an unkempt, middle-aged man appeared in front of me, suspended in the air.
I sent a wisp of qi to deactivate the formation, and a headless corpse toppled to the ground.

chapters.title: Chapter 303 – Life 76, Age 29, Martial Grandmaster Peak
chapters.content:
With the Dragon Gate Festival having concluded, the recruiters gathered their retinues and departed the Wastes. They were all, no doubt, rushing back to report on everything they had seen.
However, as these groups left, a few members from each one stayed behind. These stragglers were all low-level Grandmasters, but dressed in the clothes of common workers, they did their best to blend in with the locals.
As we already had scouts set up to monitor these people, they didn’t pose any immediate threat, but ShouLi still requested a meeting with me to discuss the situation.
“Ancestor, while dealing with these few people won’t be a problem, others have used the festival as an excuse to sneak into our territory as well. We can keep an eye on the ones that we know about, but for each spy we’ve identified, there might be two more that we haven’t. We need to do something about this.”
I sighed and jotted down a reply.
ShouLi, unless we are willing to cut off all trade with the outside world, having our territory infiltrated with spies and saboteurs is unavoidable. We can’t stop them, but we also shouldn’t worry too much about them. They are only Grandmasters, after all.
ShouLi winced. “That… might not be the case. We’ve done some testing. Anyone who has karmic energy within their bodies is barred from entering the Wastes. If a Grandmaster with karmic energy stored in their dantian tries to force their way inside, the stored energy will be violently expelled, severely injuring them in the process.
“However, once they reach Dragon Gate City, the restrictions on acquiring karmic energy disappear. If they are then assigned as the lord of a distant city, they’ll be able to accrue energy and ascend within our borders.”
I hadn’t thought of this possibility, but I should have. This was similar to how I had first gained karmic energy through the Blue Wind Pavilion. Still…
We need to consider this possibility, but until we destroy more of the formations, anyone who ascends will be trapped here. It’s a suicide mission. It seems unlikely that anyone would be willing to raise more than a handful of Lords in such a way.
As long as we are prepared, they shouldn’t be able to do much damage. Also, the spies that we know of are only low-level Grandmasters. It will take them time to ascend, and by then, we will be in an even better position to deal with them if they try to cause any trouble.
A grimace appeared on ShouLi’s face. “So, you’re saying that we shouldn’t do anything to stop them? That should just let spies roam freely about our territory?”
I’m saying that we shouldn’t be too impulsive. Killing these people would only create enmity between us and their backers. We could confront the spies we know about, but that might just result in more skilled operatives being sent in their place. Better to keep the spies we know about in place, protect ourselves from them, and feed them false information.
ShouLi appeared unhappy with this suggestion but bowed her head. “I understand, Ancestor.”
Keep track of them, though. The moment someone sends an army to attack us, kill them.
While I had a certain level of confidence in the plan that I had laid out for ShouLi, we still needed to be prepared for the worst-case scenarios.
So, how many Martial Lords could outsiders create within our territory? Combined, the Rising Sun Empire, Verdant Forest Sect, and Flowing Mountain Sect had over 300 cities within their territories. If they dedicated themselves to taking us down, they would be able to overwhelm us in only a few short years.
Worse, this was only considering the local powerhouses. If every empire on the continent began sending people into the Wastes, we would soon be overwhelmed by low-level Lords.
While this seemed unlikely, it was something we needed to be prepared for. So, with this in mind, Mo mobilized our craftsmen to shore up our defenses from threats both internal and external.
To provide for our people without needing to rely on imported supplies, our Herbalists worked on enhancing our farms, while our Illusionists provided lights for our multistory greenhouses. Alchemists concocted healing and cultivation pills, while our talisman artists crafted bundles of talismans that people could carry around for use in an emergency. The beast tamers were mostly focused on raising companions capable of fighting against Grandmasters, but they were also raising support animals, like wind horses.
However, the teams that would make the Wastes truly impregnable were the refiners and formation masters.
Within Dragon Gate City, old houses were torn down and replaced with high-density apartment buildings. While many of the residents weren’t exactly happy about this, their happiness wasn’t among our chief concerns. They were given the keys to a brand-new apartment and ample compensation for their inconvenience. If they felt that this wasn’t sufficient, then they were free to move elsewhere. This reduced Dragon Gate’s once sprawling footprint to a much more manageable size.
This story has been stolen from . If you read it on Amazon, please report it
Once this initial phase of construction was complete, GuiMing’s teams built a wall around the entire city. From then on, everyone entering was checked for ill intent via a truth stone. To prevent anyone from sneaking in, our formation masters created a series of Rank 4 defensive and detection formations around the city’s perimeter.
Of course, these precautions weren’t enough to stop everyone who might mean us harm. There was always the possibility that someone with a specialized skill set, or someone with a particularly powerful blessing, could sneak through the cracks. These defenses could only keep out the bulk of the invaders. For the rest, we would have to rely on guards equipped with the finest of Rank 3 and 4 refined equipment.
With all these defenses in place, while a group of saboteurs might be able to harm us, it would be difficult for them to cause any serious damage.
That said, we were still in a difficult position. While there were plenty of people who were willing to do whatever work was available, most of them expected to receive some form of compensation for their efforts.
Therefore, Mo worked with ShouLi to set up a contribution point system. While we could have used gold, the point system ensured that foreign powers couldn’t purchase all our resources out from under us.
For a few points, people were able to buy low-level pills and formations to help them cultivate. For a moderate price, people were able to enhance their affinities. And for a high price, they could purchase time as a nominal city lord to gather karmic energy.
This worked, for the most part. But with each year that passed, people were becoming more skilled and more capable of generating contribution points. This, in turn, had an inflationary effect on the price of essence, karmic energy, and any resources that needed to be imported from outside the Wastes.
While our herbalists could produce an endless supply of herbs, cotton, and foodstuffs, things like stone and metal were harder to come by. The Wastes had deposits of Rank 1 and 2 minerals that we could mine, but most of our Rank 3 supplies had to be imported.
This left us needing three things: essence, karmic energy, and high-level resources.
For the first, I turned to NiangBa, and for the other two, I turned to Mo.
When I looked in my inner world, I found NiangBa in a meeting with his lieutenants. This was exactly the group I needed to talk to, so I immediately dropped them a note, interrupting whatever they were discussing.
I need teams to go out into the world and gather essence. This will be like what we did in the Nine Rivers Sect, but significantly more dangerous. Back then, we had an implicit understanding with the Sovereigns. They knew what we were doing ahead of time, and the amount of essence we harvested was limited.
This time, I plan to use more powerful formations and materials capable of storing far greater quantities of essence. Additionally, with everything we are doing in the Wastes, if anyone is connected back to us, the Sovereigns will likely capture and torture them.
After reading this, NiangBa laughed and looked around at his lieutenants with a smile on his face.
“Well? You were all just complaining about being trapped in here. What do you say? Who’s ready for an adventure?”
The next day, I made my way to the western edge of the Wastes. While the north, east, and south were occupied by empire-level organizations, to the west, there was only a loose association of independent cities.
Upon my arrival at the border, I scanned the area with both my qi and soul, checking for anyone who might be watching. Once I was confident that the coast was clear, I let out the four dozen cultivators who had agreed to harvest essence for me.
NiangBa gave me a martial salute. “Don’t worry, Ancestor. You can count on us.”
After they departed, I turned my attention back to my inner world and found Mo busy at work in his office.
Mo, the clan needs access to more karmic energy. We also need channels for purchasing and importing large quantities of high-level resources without anyone knowing that we are doing it.
Mo picked up this letter, read it, and stared at it thoughtfully for several long moments.
“The guilds?”
I couldn’t help but smile.
Yes. We need to reestablish the guilds. With members in kingdoms and empires across the continent, the Blue Wind Pavilion is large enough to generate Emperor-level karma. If we can fully establish all seven guilds, we can potentially produce seven empires' worth of karmic energy.
Mo tapped his desk in thought. “That will be difficult. A Guild of Refiners would be targeted by all the major powers. Aside from that, while a single Emperor-level guild
might
be tolerated, I doubt the Sovereigns would be happy about seven ‘empires’ being controlled by a single clan.”
Start with the Guild of Alchemists. The southern empires don’t have any Pill Kings, and even Pill Lords are a rare sight. If you start the guild there, the local empires will likely support you.
The other guilds can come later. They can start in different parts of the world, at different times. Maybe have the Guild of Formation Masters start as an antagonistic response to the Guild of Alchemists.
Mo fidgeted as he thought through the possibilities and eventually let out a sigh. “Let me think through this. We can probably make it work.”
A week later, a group of alchemists left the Wastes via the southern border.
They were led by Chang, a Pill King who, in recent years, had been serving as a member of the leadership council. When he heard that a group was being sent to establish a new guild, he was the first to volunteer.ɪꜰ ʏᴏᴜ ᴡᴀɴᴛ ᴛᴏ ʀᴇᴀᴅ ᴍᴏʀᴇ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs, ᴘʟᴇᴀsᴇ ᴠɪsɪᴛ
Officially, however, their leader was one of the unassuming Grandmasters. While Chang was the one who would actually be in charge of everything, he was already a Peak King and had no need of Lord- or King-level karmic energy. Until the guild was established enough to begin generating Emperor-level energy, he would remain as nothing more than the guild’s steward.
Watching them leave, I could only hope that nothing would go wrong. Everyone was leaving the name of the Su Clan behind in the Wastes, and none of them had a history that would connect them back to us, but I didn’t know what powerful blessing might be out there that could cause problems for us.
Still, if I had learned anything from my last life, it was that the Sovereigns were patient. Whether because the Saint imposed certain rules on their actions or because they saw the entire continent as being under their complete control, the Sovereigns were willing to watch as things unfolded and only react when the time was right. If we wanted to defeat them, then we needed to take full advantage of this complacency.

chapters.title: Chapter 304 – Life 76, Age 32, Martial Grandmaster Peak
chapters.content:
With the clan rapidly expanding its influence and fixing many of the chronic issues that had plagued Dragon Gate City, karmic energy was being generated at a rapid pace. It only took four years for the first person assigned to the position of city lord to gain enough karmic energy to break through to Peak Lord. After that, a dozen people rotated into and out of the seat, each gathering enough energy to make a single breakthrough.
Once things settled down and people became used to the idea that their ‘official’ city lord would be changing on a regular basis, I signed up for a time slot as the city’s nominal lord and waited in the queue like everyone else.
I could have used my position as the clan’s ancestor to skip the line, but I wanted to keep a lower profile than that. Most people in the clan only knew that they needed to obey the order of an Ancestor Fang. Aside from the people who can come back in time with me, very few people knew that I was that elusive ‘Ancestor Fang.’ With potential hidden Lord-level assassins in play, I wanted to keep it that way.
So, instead of skipping the line, I arranged for ShouLi to have others skip the line in front of me, pushing me further back. Eventually, though, I made it to the front of the queue and spent a solid nineteen months gathering the energy needed to make the initial breakthrough to Martial Lord.
This was far longer than anyone else had needed, potentially signaling that I was somehow special and breaking my cover, but it couldn’t be helped. After I started gathering karmic energy, I noticed an anomaly and needed more energy to conduct a few experiments.
Up until this point, most of the karmic energy that I had used had come from the Nine Rivers Sect, and ever since I had purchased an affinity for karmic energy,
all
of the energy I had used had come from the sect.
That energy had always been the same. Yes, there was a difference in… potency between Lord-, King-, and Emperor-level energy, but that didn’t change the ‘feel’ of the energy. Karmic energy was karmic energy, and I had never given it much more thought than that.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
As the Lord of Dragon Gate City, however, I was personally gathering energy from a city for the first time since Eight Flower, and the energy I was getting was far from the homogenous mix that the sect had always provided me.
This energy didn’t arrive in a steady stream. Instead, it was more like discrete chunks. Each time a person had a breakthrough, or ‘their destiny changed,’ or whatever caused karmic energy to be generated happened, I received a packet of energy. Each of these chunks had its own distinct feel, but after a few months of absorbing them, I found that they could be separated into three broad categories.
The first group was what I considered ‘normal.’ Each chunk in this group was different, but none of them felt particularly special. Once in my dantian, this type of energy always combined into the same homogeneous mixture that I was used to.
The second type of energy felt more… solid. When manipulating it, I felt a deeper connection to it, and it was a bit easier to shape than normal. As far as I could tell, this second type of energy would be able to form a far better core than the first type. However, since only about a third of the energy I harvested was of this second type, it took me a year and a half to gather enough of it to form an entire core.
The final type of energy I was receiving was the scarcest. However, what this group lacked in quantity was made up for in quality. I felt an inherent connection to this energy. Even with no affinity for karmic energy at all, this energy would be easier to manipulate than the first type was with my current mid five-star affinity.
So, what was the difference between these three types of energy? I had a guess, and if necessary, I would proceed on the basis that my guess was correct. However, I decided to check with the System, just to see if it would be nice and provide me with the
true
answer.
“System, I have identified three different types of karmic energy within my dantian. I want to know why they are different.”
Cost 10 million credits.
I narrowed my eyes.
That was a relatively low cost. The System would rarely, if ever, sell me important information about the intricacies of cultivation. This made me a bit more confident that my initial guess had been correct. Still, there was no reason not to confirm it.
“Purchase.”
Purchase confirmed. 900,004,662,435 credits remaining.
There is no meaningful distinction between the three types of karmic energy that the host has identified. The only difference is the connection between the host and the person who generated the energy.
The first type was generated by someone with no connection to the host other than that of ruler and subject. The second type was generated by someone connected to the host’s body. The third type was generated by someone who is connected to both the host’s body and soul.
Credits expended. Transaction complete.
I couldn’t stop the smile that spread across my face.
In the past, Emperor Li had said that, to ascend to Martial Sovereign, I needed to rely on karmic energy generated by people connected to me through both body and soul. At the time, I hadn’t known what that meant. Even now, I was still sketchy on the details. However, this new information gave me a starting point that I could work from.
Who was generating the first type of energy? The bulk of the population of Dragon Gate City. Who was generating the second type? The people of the Su Clan.
These questions were easy enough to answer. However, who was generating the third type? The sheer fact that this third type of energy was being generated told me that there were people in Dragon Gate who were connected to me through both body and soul, but who were they?
The small amount of energy that I was getting from them suggested that their numbers were relatively small. However, that wasn’t necessarily the case. It could actually be that they had stagnated for some reason and were thus not generating any energy. But if they had a connection to my body, then they had to be members of the Su Clan. At the moment, the Su Clan was prospering. Which members of the Su Clan would be stagnant?
This story is posted elsewhere by the author. Help them out by reading the authentic version.
Framed in this way, the answer was clear: the people who had come back in time with me.
They were low in number, and nearly all of them were simply waiting around for a chance to gather karmic energy. The only ones who were able to advance were the youngsters who had yet to reach Peak Grandmaster.
This information seemed valuable. I knew that the Sovereigns used ‘blood essence’ to induct people into their clans, but I didn’t have any blood essence, and I didn’t know what it was or how to acquire it. Whatever had happened to connect these people to my soul provided me with an alternate path forward.
But… what was it? What had triggered this connection?
“System, how can I create a connection between a person and my soul?”
The cost of this information cannot be calculated at this time.
I sighed. I was on my own. After thinking through several possibilities, I sent a letter to ShouLi.
We need to make a few new rules.
I want as many of the clan’s children to be born and raised within the world orb as possible. Give the families whatever benefits you feel necessary. Tell them that children born in “Chang’an” will have higher affinities. Just do whatever is needed to get them there. I’ll provide the essence required to make this a reality.
Also, all earth cultivators need to stay in there as long as possible. They shouldn’t advance in the outside world until the conditions within the orb make it impossible to go any further.
Finally… there needs to be an initial blessing ceremony within the world orb. I know that this hasn’t worked in the past, and I don’t think anything has changed, but from now on, we need to hold an initial ceremony in the orb and then a second one outside of it.
Which, if any, of these changes would cause people to be more connected to my soul?
The first seemed most likely. Having children literally born inside of me seemed like it should create a close connection between us, but it wasn’t certain. The other two were just ideas that seemed plausible.
In any case, there was little more I could do other than wait and see what would happen. So, I turned my attention back to my advancement to Martial Lord.
While I would have liked to form a core composed of nothing but karmic energy that had been generated by the people connected to me through both body and soul, getting my clan to a state where that was feasible would take decades. So, instead, I chose to make a core using the second type of energy, energy generated by people connected to my body. This would leave me with a large reserve of karmic energy with no connection to me at all, but I would be able to use that energy for further experiments in the future.
With this settled, I sat down in my cultivation chamber to think through what I was about to do.
In the past, I had felt that something had been off about the Ruler Tier cultivation techniques I had been using. After everything I had learned in this life, I finally had a fairly good idea of what that was.
During Ranks 1 to 3, the cultivation techniques I used attuned my body to specific elemental Laws. This time, I knowingly chose to attune it to specific Laws of Metal, but even before I had known about Laws, I had still been attuning it to elemental Laws specified by whichever technique I had been using.
What about when I had advanced to Martial Lord?
None of the Rank 4 cultivation techniques I possessed were element-specific. They were all centered around karmic energy. A person’s qi was compressed to form a ‘hole in the world’ and then used to ‘break the chains,’ but the element of that qi didn’t matter.
So, if I used a standard Rank 4 cultivation technique, would I still be imbuing my body with Laws of Metal? Possibly. The element of one’s qi probably had
some
effect on the Laws involved. However, if I had to guess, then I would say that most of the Laws involved in these standard Rank 4 techniques were Laws of Karma.
That raised the question: Should I look for ways to advance to Martial Lord without karmic energy?
Again, possibly. From the experiments I had conducted on myself and others, I believed that focusing one’s cultivation base around a specific set of Laws would lead to the best outcome. A metal cultivator with a metal-based core should be more powerful than someone with a karma-based core.
However, aside from the fact that I didn’t know how to make a metal-based core, my goal in this life was to become a Sovereign. According to Emperor Li, there were no cultivation techniques that could help people ascend to that level, and the only known way to advance from Emperor to Sovereign was to flood one’s core with karmic energy.
If I didn’t start adapting my body to Laws of Karma as a Lord, would making that breakthrough to Sovereign even be possible? Maybe, but I didn’t know. So, for this life, if I wanted to make sure nothing went awry, I could only tread the well-worn path. In my next life, however, with a Sovereign-level number of credits to work with, I could explore other options.
Still, I wanted to make my core as perfect as possible. So, pulling on my reserves of Type 2 karmic energy and my karmic affinity, I set about making the best core that I could.
After creating the base of a core, I used my knowledge of refining as a guide as I built up the rest of the structure.
Like last time, this resulted in a core composed of a lace-like structure. However, the pattern of this lace was far different than it had been previously. Where the last one had been a series of connected diamonds, this was a mixture of octagons and rectangles.
Why was it different? Was it because the karmic energy I had used was different?
Instead of completing the core, I dismantled it and started again.
I created a base and then followed my instincts on how to build it out from there. This time, the result was a non-geometric pattern that looked more like flowers.
Concerned, I quickly dismantled the core and sat back in thought.
I needed to know why I had created three entirely different patterns. I could try asking the System, but it was unlikely I would get an answer. However, there might be a better way to learn what I wanted anyway.
“System, improve my technique analysis ability to Rank 4.”
Purchase confirmed. Cost 4,999,500,000 credits. 899,999,662,935 credits remaining.
Taking out a blank book, I hastily scribbled down the process of forming the core with the octagonal pattern. For the latter stages of the technique, weaving together threads of qi and karmic energy and throwing it at the ‘chains,’ I simply copied the information for a random technique in my library.
Then, I analyzed it.
Unnamed, Low-Yellow Rank 4 Cultivation Technique (Broken), Karmic Energy, Effects: Makes those connected to this core more productive. Makes those connected to this core more ambitious. Makes those connected to this core more nervous.
I quickly changed the pattern to the floral arrangement.
Unnamed, Low-Yellow Rank 4 Cultivation Technique (Broken), Karmic Energy, Effects: Makes those connected to this core more productive. Makes those connected to this core want to spend more time outdoors. Makes those connected to this core more aggravated.
With some testing, I found that the ‘Broken’ affix was because the weaves sent to break the chains didn’t match the design of the core. This was also the cause of the tertiary mental effect.
With even more testing, I found that these different lace patterns were caused by small discrepancies in the initial base that I was starting from.
After a significant amount of trial and error, I found a lace pattern that I was happy with. It was formed from a series of tightly packed irregular shapes.
Once my core was in place, I then spent even more time designing a weave for breaking chains that would complement it.
In total, this took me several years of effort, but upon seeing my final result, I felt that it was time well spent.
Core of Fellowship, Peak-Yellow Rank 4 Cultivation Technique, Karmic Energy, Effects: Makes those connected to this core feel an enhanced sense of community.

chapters.title: Chapter 305 – Life 76, Age 35, Martial Lord 1
chapters.content:
After advancing to Martial Lord, I still had a large amount of karmic energy in my dantian that I needed to get rid of. It was enough to raise two people to Martial Lord, and I knew exactly who I wanted to share it with: Mei and Murong NaYun.
Murong NaYun was nearly 280 years old. As a Grandmaster, he was nearing the end of his lifespan, and his body had already calcified 190 years ago, so advancing seemed like a dream.
Still, I wasn’t willing to give up on the man. Over the past few years, he had displayed a deep understanding of Rank 3 talisman artistry, and his work ethic had been superb. I wanted to keep him around and turn him into my Revered Elder of Lightning.
To do that, we first needed to overcome his calcification issue.
At 20% of a person’s maximum lifespan, their body would begin to stagnate. At 30%, it would calcify. This was a lesson that I had learned long ago. However, I had yet to hear any theories on the mechanism behind these changes. Stagnation and calcification were simply treated as akin to natural aging. Calcification was a natural fact of life, and few people gave it any more consideration than the fact that children grew up or the fact that people needed to eat.
But what caused stagnation? What caused calcification? I didn’t have an answer, but I did have a few clues:
After entering calcification, a cultivator could still accumulate and use qi. Calcification only affected their ability to advance. And even then, it didn’t stop people from advancing entirely. In my early lives, I had been able to slowly advance through the later levels of Martial Disciple long after calcification had set in.
Also, when I was in the Brilliant Sun Empire, I had been given a pill to ‘loosen’ my energy body. This hadn’t been enough to allow me to advance on my own, but a higher-level cultivator had been able to take hold of my qi and force it into the shape of meridians, allowing me to break through to Martial Master.
Finally, my primary focus in this life had been on how Laws affected a person’s cultivation. The premise I was working from was that by advancing my cultivation base, I was attuning my body to specific sets of Laws. Advancing in the Warrior Tier meant attuning myself to elemental Laws, and advancing as a Ruler meant attuning myself to Laws of Karma.
Putting all of this together, I came up with a hypothesis: Calcification was caused by an aging body’s inability to further adapt to new Laws. This still boiled down to ‘calcification is caused by aging,’ but it at least pointed me toward possible solutions.
There were three ways that I might be able to help Murong NaYun advance to Martial Lord: I could find a way for his body to attune to new Laws, I could figure out how to force his advancement
without
attuning his body, or I could find a way for him to advance using only the Laws that his body already possessed.
The first possibility seemed impractical. Until I had more knowledge of what it meant for a person’s body to attune to Laws, I wouldn’t have any hope of accomplishing this.
Likewise, the third possibility was questionable at best. This again came back to the idea of making a core without using karmic energy. However, it also contained the additional restriction of creating a lightning core in Murong NaYun’s body using only Warrior Tier lightning Laws.
The second possibility was the one that held the most potential. A high enough karmic affinity should allow me to control the karmic energy within another person’s body. With qi, this effect was somewhat limited since a Martial Grandmaster would typically have a high affinity for the qi they cultivated, but few, if any, people had an affinity for karmic energy.
However, I didn’t immediately leave to seek out Murong NaYun and begin such a procedure. His body, having entered calcification, created an additional layer of complexity to the task of forcibly raising him to Martial Lord. Before trying to help him, I first needed to try raising someone younger.
I didn’t want to experiment on someone who only had one life to live. If I was going to try this, it needed to be with someone who would be able to return in a future life.
Sitting down in a blank, white room, I looked at Mei. “Are you certain that you are willing to go through with this? As a Peak Grandmaster, you are able to earn contribution points and purchase karmic energy like everyone else. This experiment is a shortcut, but it has the potential to end in catastrophe.”
Mei gave me a sad smile. “Ancestor Su, over the past decade, I’ve tried my hand at every possible profession. The only one I was even able to begin learning was beast taming. And while my blessing was somewhat helpful there, without water qi, my prospects for being a talented tamer are rather limited. As a wind cultivator, it seems that I can only serve as a warrior. Unless a war breaks out, earning enough points to advance to Martial Lord will be rather challenging.”
The way Mei said this, it almost felt like she was being forced into participating in the experiment. I didn’t want that to be the case, but I wasn’t sure there was a way around it.
This tale has been unlawfully lifted from ; report any instances of this story if found elsewhere.
For our clan to function, if a person wanted to ascend to Martial Lord, then they needed to contribute to the growth and success of the clan. Ideally, everyone would have a way to make such contributions, even if their natural aptitudes were lacking. However, the unfortunate truth was that our supply of karmic energy was limited, and only those who contributed the most would be able to access it. Unless someone was a skilled Grandmaster craftsman, it would be difficult for them to ascend.
Still, even if some people would find earning contribution points difficult, Mei shouldn’t have been one of them.
“You may not be a skilled craftsman, but with your blessing, you would make an excellent steward. I can talk to ShouLi about arranging such a position for you. With your blessing, I’m sure you will be able to earn enough contribution points to ascend in no time.”
Mei let out a wry chuckle. “Sadly, no. I have already tried such things, and my blessing has done nothing but sabotage me.”
The corner of Mei’s lips rose in a wistful smirk. “As a child, I had a bit of training in city management, and I thought that I could make certain contributions there. Using the soul cultivation technique you taught me, I have mostly been able to suppress my blessing’s impulses, but every now and then, they force their way through. Whenever that happens, I do something to sabotage myself.”
I wrinkled my brow in concern as Mei pressed on.
“It became clear to me that my blessing doesn’t want me participating in such tasks. I had thought that it wouldn’t allow me to advance to Lord at all, but instead, it seems to have wanted me here. So, please, Ancestor Su, perform your experiment. It is likely the only way that I will ever be allowed to advance to Martial Lord.”
I closed my eyes and nodded. “Alright.”
Folding my hands on my lap, I turned my concentration inward. “Do your best to relax. I am going to try to inject your body with karmic energy.”
I pulled on the energy in my dantian, directed it through my meridians, and out the acupoints in my lower arms. I then tried to direct it toward Mei, but the moment it entered the open air, it evaporated.
Sighing, I opened my eyes and looked at her. “Please hold out your arm.”
When she did, I took hold of her wrist and overlapped the open acupoint there with the one in my palm. This time, when I pulled karmic energy through my acupoint, it only had to travel a small distance before entering Mei’s energy body, so it didn’t have time to dissipate.
With this success, I channeled more karmic energy out of my body, pushed it into Mei’s, directed it through her meridians, and forced it to pool in her dantian.
During this process, Mei didn’t say a word. She sat stock-still, eyes open in shock.
Once enough energy was inside her dantian, I retracted my hand.
“Try manipulating the energy yourself. See if you can shape it into a ball.”
Following my instructions, Mei gradually formed the energy into the rough shape of a core. I wasn’t certain, but from what I could tell, her control over the energy matched what I would normally expect.
“Alright.” I took a deep breath. “For this next part, it would work best if I place a hand on your dantian.”
Mei smiled warmly at me. “Of course, Ancestor Su.”
She scooted her chair closer to me and placed her hands on her armrests.
Closing my eyes once more, I reached out, placed a palm on her abdomen, and focused on the energy that I had recently injected into her. Instinctively, her body recoiled and tried to fight against my control, but without any affinity for karmic energy, there was nothing she could do.
Working as quickly as I could, I shaped the energy into a pattern of the Core of Fellowship.
Once I was done, I pulled back my hand and nodded. Then, I took out a Rank 4 Qi Gathering Formation and several Rank 3 Qi Gathering Pills. “Alright, the next step is to fill that core to the brim with your qi.”
As I had already given Mei a high wind affinity, this wasn’t something that I could help with, but my help wasn’t needed. In less than a week, she had gathered the qi she needed and was ready for a breakthrough.
At that point, I placed a hand back on her abdomen and created a weave of karmic energy. Then, I instructed Mei on how to weave her wind qi into it.
As soon as this was done, she pushed a final bit of qi into her core, opening a hole in the world, and, together, we pushed the weave of energy through, breaking one of her chains and allowing her to ascend to Martial Lord.
Mei opened her eyes, and tears of happiness welled up within them. She jumped to her feet and hugged me. “Thank you.”
I patted her on the back awkwardly. “You’re welcome.”
With Mei having served as a proof of concept, I sought out Murong NaYun and explained the process to him. Not caring about the details or risks involved, he agreed to immediately proceed with his breakthrough attempt.
This time, as I tried to shove karmic energy into Grandmaster Murong’s body, I was met with a great deal of resistance. It didn’t take me long to conclude that trying to guide it all the way through his arm and into his torso would severely damage his meridians.
So, instead, I placed a hand on his abdomen and injected the karmic energy through the acupoint closest to his dantian.
Once it was all in place, constructing a core for him was a bit arduous, and from the look on his face, it was rather painful, but there were no surprises. Injecting the core with sufficient karmic energy to create a hole in the world, however, wasn’t so easy.
Instead of using just a Rank 4 Qi Gathering Formation, Grandmaster Murong needed a Rank 6 formation. This wasn’t because he needed more qi. It was because he needed the formation to provide pressure to help him shove energy into his new core.
After nearly a month of hard work, he finally reached the point where he was ready for his breakthrough, and, working together, we managed to break one of the chains binding him.
Upon feeling his ascension to Martial Lord, like Mei, Murong NaYun burst out in tears of joy. However, instead of hugging me, he only gave me a deep bow. “Thank you, Ancestor Su.”Thɪs updatᴇd by NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
With Mei and Murong NaYun, I had learned a valuable skill: transferring karmic energy from myself to someone else.
I found the current Lord of Dragon Gate, and after securing a few promises, he allowed me to experiment with pulling karmic energy from his body and storing it within myself. This was a bit trickier since his body instinctively wanted to cling to the energy, but the basic premise was the same. So, it only took me a few minutes to get the hang of it.
Once I did, I couldn't help but grin like a madman. I was two steps closer to replicating the way the Sovereign Clans were able to store and distribute karmic energy.

chapters.title: Chapter 306 – Life 76, Age 39, Martial Lord 3
chapters.content:
With my newfound understanding of karmic energy, I had ShouLi implement a series of reforms to how we sold and managed the valuable resource.
We substantially lowered the cost of purchasing a stint as a nominal city lord, but at the same time, we implemented a rule that city lords would only be allowed to keep a third of whatever karmic energy they harvested. Each year, I would visit the acting city lord and extract any karmic energy generated by members of the Su Clan. I would also extract roughly half of the energy generated by outsiders.
I kept the Su Clan energy for myself, and ShouLi sold off the rest at a slight markup. Because of this, if anyone used the rotation of our city lords to judge how many Martial Lords we had, they would end up severely underestimating us.
After I reached Peak Lord, we would begin selling off the Su Clan energy as well, though at a much steeper markup. Was using such energy when advancing as a Ruler beneficial? Maybe not, but I wanted to use it just in case, and I was certain that many people in my clan would feel the same way.
With this new structure in place, I returned to my study of Laws and cultivation techniques.
Before long, the nine new cities surrounding Dragon Gate were fully operational. While their defenses might not have been impenetrable, they were at the limit of what our Formation Lords could accomplish, considering the sparse qi levels in the Wastes.
Shortly after this, the bones of ten more cities were constructed around Rosehill, and ten more were started around Mount Jiang. Before these cities could generate karmic energy, we would need to increase their populations substantially, but their mere existence was enough for the moment.
These cities, with their powerful defensive formations, would serve as a shield to protect us from any invasions. And with our flanks secure, we were ready to unlock the next section of the Wastes.
The primary danger in the cavern beneath the Rosehill Hot Springs was the immense heat generated by its spirit fire. Without access to qi, the only people who would be able to survive in the area surrounding the cavern’s formation were Rank 3 body cultivators. And even within that group, only a select few would be able to break the formation’s outer ring.
To break the formation beneath the Su Clan, we had needed to destroy five white gems. Because these gems had been infused with metal energy, they were incredibly sturdy, and to even damage them, TongBin had first needed to infuse them with fire wu.
To break the Rosehill formation, we would need to destroy five dark blue, water-infused gems around its perimeter. And since these gems would likely need to be infused with earth wu before they could be damaged, this was a job that only an earth body cultivator could accomplish.Googlᴇ search ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
Like with the formation under the Su Clan, a single cultivator should be enough to make this happen, but the fact that the formation was surrounded by a lake of lava worried me. So, we sent a team of five Peak Rank 3 earth body cultivators just to be safe. Working together, they would be able to shatter all five gems at once and, hopefully, escape before the changes to the formation affected the surrounding lava.
After sending this team on its mission, I joined a group of Martial Lords and waited at the border between Dragon Gate City and the Rosehill Hot Springs.
The wait was interminable.
Hours passed one after the other.
It wasn’t until sixteen hours after the team of earth cultivators had set out that a powerful earthquake rocked the Wastes. When this earthquake subsided, a brilliant shimmer appeared in the air, high above Rosehill.
This shimmer lasted for only a moment, and once it was gone, the group of Lords I was with looked around at their leader. The younger man nodded silently, took a deep breath, and cautiously walked toward Rosehill with both hands extended.
At first, he slowed down with each step, but after passing the 10-meter mark without obstruction, he began to speed up.
As soon as it was clear that we would be able to enter Rosehill’s territory, he turned around and waved.
Upon receiving this signal, the earth cultivators among us raced forward at a blistering pace, eager to begin enhancing the territory’s defenses before outsiders could take advantage of this opportunity and invade.
I was in an even greater hurry than these earth cultivators, but as I had yet to cultivate my body, if I wanted to travel at the swiftest possible speed, I was relegated to using a carriage.
Still, I needed to hurry. If I didn’t, I would miss an important meeting with an old acquaintance. Opening up Rosehill had taken longer than I had hoped, and I was almost out of time.
As I approached the western edge of the Wastes, I carefully scanned my surroundings for any signs that I was being watched. Twice, I noticed a small anomaly in the flow of environmental qi. These might have been nothing, but with Emperors and Sovereigns in play, I didn’t want to take any chances, so I took detours to avoid them.
A case of content theft: this narrative is not rightfully on Amazon; if you spot it, report the violation.
When I was only a step away from losing the protection of the Wastes’ formation, a black portal suddenly appeared in front of me.
The first person to walk out of this portal was RuLan. Upon seeing me, she cupped her fists in a martial salute. “Greetings, Senior Brother.”
While RuLan appeared normal enough, I could sense a deep sadness hidden beneath her cheery façade.
Understanding the seriousness of the situation, I saluted her back. “Greetings, Junior Sister.”
Then, she stepped to the side, and a decaying old man walked out of the portal. His elegant blue robes looked two sizes too big, and his skin hung loosely from his bones. However, his body was still filled with an indescribable aura of power.
Upon seeing me, he let out a light snort. “You finally decided to make your appearance, you unfilial disciple.”
I cupped my fists and bowed to him. “Greetings, Emperor Li.”
He waved a dismissive hand. “We don’t have much time. Send RuLan away before she’s noticed.”
I moved to do as he said, but before I could, RuLan held up a hand to stop me. She turned and gave Emperor Li a deep bow. “Thank you for your training, Master. I will do my best to make you proud.”
As she stood back upright, tears flowed down her face.
Emperor Li just grunted. “Don’t cry, girl. We’ll see each other again. Though, at that time, I might be the one saying goodbye to you. Spend these years well. Live them without regret.”
She bowed again. “Yes, Master.”
Seeing their conversation was at an end, I flicked a finger and sent RuLan into my inner world.
The grandfatherly look on Emperor Li’s face vanished, and a predatory glint appeared in his eyes. He looked me up and down, appraising me. “So, you’re finally ready to become a Sovereign.”
I nodded silently.
The corners of Li’s mouth turned up in a wolfish grin. “Good. With any luck, I’ll finally be allowed to leave this wretched place.”
Suddenly, Li looked up and stared into the distance.
“Our time is almost up.” His head dropped, and he looked me in the eye. “You don’t need to worry about the breakthrough to King. No one is going to send their Lords into this deathtrap. Once the Wastes is open to Emperors, however, you will need to be a lot more careful. As for the final breakthrough to Sovereign, make sure that you are fully prepared. The moment you
advance
, they will come for you.”
Without waiting for me to respond, Emperor Li walked back through his portal.
Worried that someone might be on their way, I turned around and fled deeper into the Wastes at the fastest possible speed.
Taking Emperor Li’s words to heart, I talked to ShouLi about accelerating our plans.
Having been trapped within my inner world for over two decades, ShouLi had been unable to advance her cultivation base, so, instead, she had spent every spare minute trying to understand what needed to be done to advance to Rank 4 of body cultivation. We now needed that knowledge if we wanted any hope of unlocking the section of the formation.
While her research wasn’t exactly complete, it was complete enough for her to attempt a breakthrough.
So, without informing anyone of our plans, I slipped out of the Wastes and snuck into a small village along its northern border. Once I was hidden inside someone’s rundown barn, I set up an anti-eavesdropping formation and pulled out ShouLi, Liang, NiangBa, and several other body cultivators.
As everyone was already aware of our purpose, Liang and the others formed a semicircle around ShouLi without needing me to prompt them.
I walked up to ShouLi and placed a hand on her abdomen. “Relax your mind.”
Then, I pushed all my stored-up Su Clan karmic energy into her dantian.
ShouLi took a deep breath and sat down in the lotus position.
She looked at me, and I handed her a storage bag.
Opening it, she pulled out a hunk of raw meat from a Rank 4 demon beast.
After a shiver of disgust, she started eating.
With each bite, she pulled a thread of karmic energy from her core and infused it into the meat.
When the meat reached her stomach, her blessing extracted the combination of wu and karmic energy and infused it into her skin.
ShouLi then directed this energy into her tendons, her bones, and finally, into her muscles.
This process continued, one bite after another. After eating nearly three kilos of raw meat, something within ShouLi snapped. Her muscles rippled violently, and black oil oozed out of her pores.
She turned to look up at Liang, but before she could, her body froze in shock as an enlightenment poured into her. When it was over, she slumped to the ground.
With a nod of satisfaction, I sent everyone back into my inner world, dismantled the formation, and headed back into the Wastes.
While creating an entirely new cultivation technique was difficult, ShouLi had benefited greatly from the assistance of her blessing. It had been able to extract the energy of the raw beast meat and convert it into an ideal power source for her advancement. Taking her technique and transforming it into something usable by the entire clan, however, was a different challenge entirely.
The key to making her technique work had been a realization that when a demon beast died, the karmic energy in its body evaporated while the demonic energy remained behind. By infusing the raw meat with new energy, ShouLi had used a shortcut to create the proper blend of demonic and karmic energy.
This was why she had needed to eat the meat raw. Cooking it would have disrupted the demonic energy, causing the infusion process to fail.
However, without ShouLi’s blessing, none of this would have worked. Trace amounts of incompatible demonic energy in the beast meat would act as potent impurities, poisoning anyone else who tried this. Additionally, small-scale tests proved that absorbing karmic energy from meat was far more difficult than ShouLi made it look. Without a proper cultivation technique, it was, essentially, impossible.
That said, for every problem, there was a solution.
I was of the belief that there had to be a way to reach Rank 4 in body cultivation without relying on beast meat. However, even if there was, such a method would take several more decades to develop. So, instead, our clan focused on raising beasts within enclosures that had been flooded with only a single type of wu. This negatively impacted their growth, but it prevented them from absorbing any impurities.
As this had been one of the first initiatives ShouLi set up after our takeover of the Su Clan, several beasts had already reached Rank 3 and were nearly ready for harvest.
In contrast, creating a cultivation technique that would allow a person to draw karmic energy from meat was far more challenging. But with the enlightenment she had received, ShouLi was able to piece together what needed to be done.
So, five years after ShouLi’s initial breakthrough, we returned to that abandoned barn, and Liang and NiangBa became the next two people to advance to Rank 4 in body cultivation.
After that, it was only a matter of time before we would be ready to take down the next ring of Dragon Gate City’s formation and allow people to advance to King.

chapters.title: Chapter 307 – Life 76, Age 48, Martial Lord Peak
chapters.content:
Before we could unlock the second ring under Dragon Gate, we needed a Peak Rank 4 fire body cultivator. Even with a cultivation technique in place and ample karmic energy being generated by our guilds and cities, this still took time.
But that was fine. We had plenty of other tasks that needed to get done in the meantime, such as populating the cities around Rosehill. Even with the council offering various incentives to get people to immigrate from the independent cities west of the Wastes, this was taking time.
I wanted to advance to Martial King, and the Martial Kings in my inner world wanted a chance to get out and stretch their legs, but we all understood the dangers of rushing.
Eventually, though, Peak Rank 4 body cultivators began to make their appearance, and we were ready to take the next step forward.
As Emperor Li had predicted, even though Lords could now enter our territory through our western border, none did. No armies appeared on the horizon, and none of the known spies within our cities advanced to Martial Lord. So, once everything was in place, we pushed forward and sent a team of metal cultivators to break the outer ring of the formation beneath Mount Jiang.
As we had known both the location and status of this formation for over a decade, we knew exactly what needed to be done to break it. Less than a day after the order was given, the task was complete.
After that, a team of formation specialists rushed in to shore up our defenses while the rest of us turned our sights toward the sects.
SuYin was stationed in the Verdant Fields Sect, and Cao MeiLan was in the Twin Mountains Sect. They had both advanced to Peak Grandmaster and become elders in their respective sects, but neither had been able to infiltrate their sect’s core leadership team. So, I called them back to Dragon Gate, gave them an infusion of karmic energy, and provided them with a manual for cultivating the Core of Fellowship.
Then, while Cao and SuYin studied this technique, I handed my System-purchased identity jades to a couple of Formation Grandmasters and sent them to find the main node of the sects’ Mountain-Protecting Formations.
These were Rank 4 formations, and I had only been able to send Grandmasters to study them, so I hadn’t expected them to be able to do too much. This was only intended as a preliminary investigation. At best, I was hoping that they would be able to produce a few extra identity tokens.
However, with only a glance, these Grandmasters were able to identify severe flaws in both formations. Without even needing my help, they were able to craft keys capable of permanently shutting down the defenses of both sects.
At first, this seemed strange. Why would the Mountain-Protecting Formations have such major flaws in them? But then, I remembered what had happened back when I was a Grandmaster in the Twin Mountains Sect. These flaws were intentional. They were there so that the parent sects could disable the formations whenever they chose. Unfortunately for them, it also allowed us to develop that same ability.
A couple of months later, SuYin and Cao advanced to Martial Lord.
After sending warnings to our people embedded in the sects, we simultaneously dispatched a team of body cultivators to both the Twin Mountains and the Verdant Fields. As both sects had already moved their fire seeds, the formation caverns beneath them held little danger. So, less than a day later, the restrictions stopping Lords from entering the sects’ territories dropped.
Leading a group of Peak Lords, SuYin swiftly invaded the Verdant Fields while Cao led a group to the Twin Mountains. Because they had detailed layouts for their respective sects, they were able to attack the sects’ leadership without alerting anyone else to their presence. The Grandmasters in charge of these sects were barely able to muster any resistance.
A few of the elders who had focused on martial combat chose to sacrifice themselves in a mad display of defiance, but most of the sects’ leadership capitulated without a fight. Less than an hour after the invasions began, SuYin was named the new Sect Master of the Verdant Fields, and Cao was named the new Sect Master of the Twin Mountains.
This caused a bit of turmoil, but few people truly cared who the Sect Master was. All that mattered was power and benefits. When SuYin and Cao showed off their Lord-level cultivation bases and promised the elders that they, too, would have a chance at advancement, nearly all of them instantly abandoned the darkness to join the light.
Once the situation in the sects was stable, I grabbed TongBin—who had advanced to Peak Rank 4 in fire body cultivation—and a random Lord-level earth cultivator, and we headed down to the cavern beneath Dragon Gate.
Originally, this cavern had been shrouded in the mists of a purple miasma. After destroying the formation’s outer ring, a shield had appeared to prevent us from damaging the formation further, and the miasma became trapped within the confines of that shield.
With the outer rings of all five formations now destroyed, that shield had vanished. However, the miasma hadn’t seeped back out to encompass the entire cavern. It was still concentrated in the area around the formation.
I handed TongBin a jade box inscribed with a complex formation. “First things first. Let’s get rid of that fire seed.”

TongBin didn’t hesitate. He walked over to the edge of the formation, looked up at the fire seed that was suspended in the air 30 meters above him, and jumped.
I worried that the formation might make things difficult for the man, but he grabbed the fire seed and stuffed it into the jade box without issue. Then, after closing the box securely, TongBin landed deftly on the other side of the cavern.
With the fire seed gone, the earth essence gathered by the formation was pouring upward toward the surface without interference. So, I reached into my inner world and pulled out a 5-meter-thick, 20-meter-wide slab of olivine.
I looked at the earth cultivator. “We need to attach this to the cavern’s ceiling so that it completely covers the formation. Since the formation will stop you from using your qi, you won’t be able to bond it in the center, so just focus on attaching the edges to the ceiling as firmly as possible.”
As a Martial Lord, moving such a large block of olivine shouldn’t have been too difficult for the man, but restrictions imposed by the cavern’s formation posed unique challenges. Also, as neither he nor I were body cultivators, we both had to be exceedingly cautious of the concentrated miasma that still lingered in the cavern.
Still, with a little assistance from TongBin, we were able to get the stone into position, and the earth cultivator melded it into the ceiling. From then on, all the essence pouring out of the formation would be stored in that slab of olivine. We would just need to come down and harvest it before it overflowed.
With this task complete, I nodded to TongBin. “Do it.”
He gave me a short bow and then raced to the edge of the formation.
After finding the five white gems embedded around its perimeter, he shattered each of them with only a single punch. This time, with his karma-infused muscles, he hadn’t even needed to corrupt them with fire wu.
When the last gem shattered, the cavern shook as a violent earthquake rocked the Wastes. We didn’t run, though. Our earth cultivator could protect us if the cavern collapsed, and I wanted to make sure that the quake didn’t damage the newly placed olivine slab.
A few minutes later, the shaking settled down, and I smiled at my companions. “Good job.”
With the second ring of the formation destroyed, Dragon Gate City became the center of the new Dragon Gate Kingdom. While the actual square footage of this kingdom was somewhat limited, we had been able to cram enough people inside of it to generate King-level karmic energy.
Before worrying about anything else, I first took teams to each of the formation caverns, removed the fire seeds, and attached minerals to the ceilings to capture all the gathered essence.The most update n0vels are published on
Because of this, neither the hole at the center of the Verdant Fields Sect nor the underground pools in the Twin Mountains Sect could be used to raise people’s affinities. From here on, the sects were completely under our control. Those who contributed to our clan’s growth would be given opportunities to raise their affinities. Those who didn’t would find their path cut short.
With this settled, I returned to a life of seclusion and study as the clan around me expanded at a rapid rate.
ShouLi’s priorities shifted to focusing on unlocking the secrets of Rank 5 body cultivation, and her lieutenants stepped forward to take control of our fledgling empire. Their main goal was to grow our population as quickly as possible. Without enough people to generate King-level karmic energy, there was no reason to unlock more of the Wastes’ formations.
At first, this was looking like it might take an interminable amount of time, but before long, the clan’s leadership stumbled upon a solution: the sects.
Asking people in one city to leave their homes and travel hundreds of kilometers just to live in a different city was a difficult proposition. Even when offered generous compensation, few people were willing to agree. After all, pies didn’t fall from the sky. If someone was willing to promise lavish rewards, there had to be a catch.
Sects, however, were different. Everyone knew that sects recruited and trained skilled disciples. So, when recruiters from the Twin Mountains Sect showed up, showcased their abilities, and stated that they were only willing to accept the ten most talented individuals from a town or city, people fought each other for the chance to join.
At first, we only sent recruiters to the independent cities west of the Wastes. However, when the strategy proved successful, we began sending recruiters to towns and villages across the entirety of the western half of the continent.
Most towns welcomed our recruiters. Usually, children from wealthy mortal families with low affinities and poor aptitudes could only dream of joining a sect. We were making that dream a reality. While most of these children might never return home, these families were still willing to send their children away in the hope that they would one day come back as talented alchemists.
However, while many were excited by the opportunities we offered, some forces were not exactly thrilled by stealing away their population base, so disputes would sometimes arise. The most vicious of these disputes was between the recruiters of the Twin Mountains Sect and the members of the Guild of Alchemists.
As a new power that had recently risen up in the southern empires, the Guild of Alchemists was fiercely protective of its reputation as the premier organization for the learning and study of alchemy. So, when an unknown sect popped up and started recruiting disciples out from under it, the guild was none too pleased.
This started a long-running feud, with members of both groups constantly challenging the other side to alchemy duels. However, instead of one side or the other being suppressed, this feud only helped the reputations of both groups grow. After only a few years, everyone in the southern empires was familiar with both the sect and the guild.
With the Twin Mountains Sect’s accomplishments as a guide, the Verdant Fields Sect also expanded its recruitment efforts. This, in turn, caused the Guild of Alchemists to assist in the creation of a Guild of Herbalists.
A few years later, the leadership council chose to transform the cities around Rosehill and Mount Jiang into the Rosehill Sect and the Mount Jiang Sect. The Mount Jiang Sect would focus on beast taming, and the Rosehill Sect would focus on refining.
As a sect focused on refining was anathema to nearly every empire on the continent, the creation of the Rosehill Sect stirred up a great deal of controversy, and its recruiters were unable to leave the Wastes without being killed or captured. When this didn’t make us back down, the continent’s various empires began targeting the recruiters from our other sects as well.
However, while this severely curtailed our active recruitment efforts, the notoriety of our sects continued to spread. Metal cultivators from around the continent traveled to the Wastes to study their craft in peace, and this, in turn, caused cultivators of the other elements to join them.
Eventually, the leadership council set up three more sects in the northwest, northeast, and southeast of the Wastes. These were focused on illusions, talismans, and formations. Their Sect Masters were my Revered Elders: Meng LuYao, Murong NaYun, and Shi YuLong.
This gave us a total of eight kingdoms slowly growing within the confines of the Wastes.

chapters.title: Chapter 308 – Life 76, Age 54, Martial Lord Peak
chapters.content:
Dragon Gate Kingdom was producing enough karmic energy for a Lord to break through to King once every 8 months. At this rate, a King 1 could advance to King 2 in only 4 months, and a King 9 could advance to Peak King in about 9 months. This meant that Dragon Gate Kingdom was producing enough karmic energy for a person to ascend from Peak Lord to Peak King in a little over 5 years.
Compared to the other kingdoms on the continent, this was rather impressive. For our needs, however, it was only a drop in the bucket. We had dozens of Lords who were waiting for their chance to ascend, ShouLi and others needed King-level energy to experiment with Rank 5 body cultivation, and our beast tamers needed King-level energy to breed Rank 5 beasts.
Therefore, we split the karmic energy into 5 portions. The current acting city lord was allowed to keep the first portion. The second was reserved for any Lords wanting to breakthrough to King, and the third was for Kings who were looking to advance. The fourth and fifth portions were for the body cultivators and the beast tamers.
With only Dragon Gate Kingdom supplying us with King-level energy, splitting it in 5 different directions like this meant that anyone who wanted energy would need to wait an excessively long amount of time. However, once the population bases of the Twin Mountains Sect, the Guild of Alchemists, and the Guild of Formation Specialists reached the point where these organizations could start producing King-level energy as well, this would no longer be much of a concern. Then, once even more of our sects and guilds were able to start producing energy, it wouldn’t be any issue at all.
That said, balancing the various interests of the different groups involved was somewhat tricky. Ideally, all of the karmic energy we harvested would flow to members of the Su Clan, but that would cause fewer people to be willing to join us, and that would cause our karmic energy generation to plummet. So, ShouLi, the guild leaders, and the Sect Masters had to find a balance between helping our people and helping the people who joined us.
Thankfully, though, as the clan’s ancestor, I had no place in these conversations. I just needed to focus on cultivation and look for ways to increase the clan’s overall strength.
While the sects and guilds were great for generating large amounts of King-level energy, there was one major problem with them. Almost none of their members were from the Su Clan, so the karmic energy they generated was generic energy that had no connection to either my body or soul.
I had no reason to believe that using this energy while advancing as a King would be a problem. As a Lord, I had only used energy generated from members of the Su clan, and I hadn’t noticed any real benefit to doing so. However, on the off chance that it might be important during my ascension to Martial Sovereign, I wanted to keep it up.
So, even as karmic energy flowed in from multiple directions, I focused only on slowly accumulating the small portion of energy that was generated by members of my clan. Because of this, it took me nearly two years to accumulate enough energy for my initial breakthrough to Martial King.
Once I was ready, I entered seclusion and focused on upgrading my Core of Fellowship.
With my knowledge and experience, I was confident that I could develop a Rank 5 technique equal to what I had done in Rank 4. There was just one problem: if I made any mistakes, it would be incredibly difficult to fix them.
When developing the Rank 4 version of the Core of Fellowship, I had constructed several partial cores, but because I didn’t complete them, I had been able to disassemble them without issue.
To advance to King, I would need to upgrade the core that I already had. If I made a mistake in this process, I might need to somehow disassemble my entire core to fix it, and I wasn’t sure if that was even possible. So, to try and prevent any problems from cropping up, I wanted to advance my karmic affinity as much as possible before advancing.
At the moment, I had a low five-star affinity, and because of the insane multiplier involved, permanently increasing this affinity was out of the question. That didn’t mean I was out of options, however.
“System, give me a temporary boost to my karmic affinity that will last only for the remainder of this life. Raise it to peak five-star.”
Purchase confirmed. Cost 150 billion credits. 749,999,662,935 credits remaining.
A tingling sensation filled me. Then, as it subsided, I stretched my senses to see if there was any hint of the nervousness that I had felt in the past. Thankfully, no such feeling presented itself.
That being the case, I focused on the task at hand: crafting a Rank 5 core.
First, I infused my existing core with King-level energy. Then, once it was saturated, I slowly extended the energy outward, creating a secondary lattice that wrapped around the first.
I had no reason to rush, so I took my time and made each strand of this new lace lattice as dense and as thin as possible.
In total, crafting my new core took over two years of nearly constant effort. This was significantly longer than I had spent in past lives. However, because I took things slowly, I made fewer mistakes, and when I did make a mistake, I caught it early enough that I could fix it without needing to dismantle everything.
Once my core was complete, I then worked up upgrading the weave of qi and karmic energy used for shattering the chains while ascending.
If you come across this story on Amazon, be aware that it has been stolen from . Please report it.
After another year, I was somewhat confident in my creation, but without any way to verify it, I was hesitant to use it. So, taking a deep breath to fortify my nerves, I chose to spend the majority of my remaining credits on enhancing my appraisal ability.
“System, improve my technique analysis ability to Rank 5.”
Purchase confirmed. Cost 495 billion credits. 254,998,662,935 credits remaining.
Then, I scribbled down a set of instructions into a blank book and examined it.
Core of Fellowship, High-Yellow Rank 5 Cultivation Technique (Broken), Karmic Energy, Effects: Makes those connected to this core feel an enhanced sense of community. Makes those connected to this core feel a slight sense of unease.
I couldn’t help but grin. It had been expensive, but upgrading that ability had been the right call.
Over the next month, I made continual refinements to the technique until I produced exactly what I was looking for.
Core of Fellowship, Peak-Yellow Rank 5 Cultivation Technique, Karmic Energy, Effects: Makes those connected to this core feel an enhanced sense of community.
Once it was complete, I was ready to begin advancing.
While I was focused on ascending to Martial King, ShouLi, Liang, NiangBa, and others were all focused on figuring out the secrets to Rank 5 of body cultivation. Without a source of King-level karmic energy, they hadn’t been able to do much, but with energy now pouring in from several different sources, advancing had become their sole focus.
This dedication may have been the result of madness induced by their body or soul cultivation. Alternatively, it may have simply been a natural drive to grow stronger. In my mind, though, the most likely explanation was that they knew that reaching Peak Rank 5 of body cultivation would allow them to shatter the third ring of the Wastes’ formations. This would allow Emperors to enter the Wastes, and they would no longer be stuck hiding within my inner world.
Whatever the case may be, their dedication was commendable, and it didn’t take long for this dedication to pay off. Before I could even complete my ascension to Martial King, ShouLi requested a trip to the barn along the Wastes’ northern border.
In truth, her plan to advance from Rank 4 to Rank 5 wasn’t exactly complicated. The biggest challenge had been raising a demon beast to Rank 5. Once that was done, the beast was slaughtered, and we were on our way.
After arriving in the barn, I again set up an anti-eavesdropping formation. Then, I pulled out our high-level body cultivators, and ShouLi sat down to begin her advancement.
As I and a group of body cultivators watched in horrid fascination, ShouLi took large hunks of raw Rank 5 beast meat, infused them with King-level karmic energy, and consumed them.
