Like last time, ShouLi’s blessing pulled the energy from this meat and infused it into her skin. Then, she pulled it out and threaded it through her body. From her skin to her tendons. From her tendons to her bones. From her bones to her muscles. And, finally, from her muscles to her nervous system.
When she had advanced to Rank 4, a copious amount of thick, black oil had streamed out of her pores. This time, though, since the volume of her nervous system was significantly smaller than the volume of her muscles, only a thin layer of that black oil had appeared.
After advancing, ShouLi received her next round of enlightenment. Then, I pulled everyone back into my inner world and rushed away.
Once within my inner world, NiangBa looked at ShouLi with a cunning glint in his eyes. Without needing him to say a single word, ShouLi nodded and followed him to the arena.
In an all-out fight, ShouLi wouldn’t have stood a chance against NiangBa. Only earth qi could be used in my inner world, and NiangBa was an earth cultivator while ShouLi was a water cultivator. With her body cultivation and an Emperor-level will-lock, ShouLi wasn’t exactly defenseless, but there was no way she would be able to defeat someone like NiangBa.
They weren’t heading to the arena for an all-out fight, though.
Once there, they bowed to each other and took up fighting stances.
Then, at nearly the exact same moment, they rushed forward.
As they neared each other, both combatants readied their punches.
They both struck out at the same time, and their fists collided.
This caused NiangBa to be pushed back two meters while ShouLi was pushed back only one.
ShouLi was stronger, but not
that
much stronger.
Then, they rushed forward once more.
This time, though, upon seeing NiangBa make his move, ShouLi quickly reoriented, shifted her weight, and swung a leg at his midsection.
ShouLi’s strike landed before NiangBa could even react, and he was sent rocketing backward.
When he finally came to a stop, NiangBa grinned wildly. “It worked?”
ShouLi just nodded and prepared for her next attack.
With Ranks 1 to 3 of body cultivation, a person’s body became more resilient. After a person toughened their skin, tendons, and bones, they were nearly impervious to mortal weapons. If a Peak Rank 3 body cultivator were struck with a steel sword, they would remain unscathed, and the sword would end up bent and broken. Only a refined weapon at or above Rank 3 would have any chance of harming them.
However, while their defenses might have been impressive, their offensive prowess was rather lackluster. The only real offensive advantage to being a Rank 3 body cultivator was that one would be able to attack without worrying about taking damage in the process.The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
With Rank 4, a person refined their muscles, and things changed. They would be able to run hundreds of miles without tiring, leap dozens of meters into the air, and punch with enough strength to shatter even low-level Rank 4 refined armor.
Again, though, there was a problem. While ascending to Rank 4 enhanced a person’s muscles, it also caused problems with lack of control. A person might have had incredible strength, but making use of that strength in a fast-paced battle was incredibly difficult.
So, during her advancement to Rank 5, ShouLi had enhanced her nervous system.
The fight between ShouLi and NiangBa continued for several more minutes, but ShouLi’s advantage was obvious. NiangBa wasn’t that much weaker than her, but he couldn’t land a single strike.
So, NiangBa shifted his tactics.
He wrapped a layer of dirt with earth qi, compressed it into a hardened spike, and shot it toward ShouLi’s back.
Since he had only used Grandmaster-level energy, ShouLi was easily able to pivot and smash the spike apart with a single blow.
NiangBa shot out a spike using Lord-level energy. The result was the same.
It was only when he used King-level energy to compress and harden a spike that ShouLi could no longer smash it with a single punch. However, because the spike was so large and dense, its speed was lacking, and ShouLi was easily able to dodge it.
After a few more tests, NiangBa covered himself in stone and went on the attack.
This stone armor enhanced both his offense and defense but reduced his speed. With this armor in place, ShouLi could easily strike him, but by tanking her blows, he was able to land a few hits of his own.
In the end, while NiangBa limited his strength to that of a low-level King, he still had the energy reserves of an Emperor and was able to wear ShouLi down.
Still, while she lost the fight, ShouLi was happy. By standing toe-to-toe with NiangBa without the use of any qi, she had been able to prove the efficacy of body cultivation.

chapters.title: Chapter 309 – Life 76, Age 72, Martial King Peak
chapters.content:
After ShouLi advanced to Rank 5 of body cultivation, it wasn’t long before others began racing to join her.
The first hurdle that needed to be overcome was adapting ShouLi’s Rank 5 technique so that someone without her blessing would be able to use it. In the past, this had been a challenge, but with the experience that our body cultivators had in modifying her previous techniques, it was rather straightforward.
In only a few years, this task was complete, and we just needed to wait for the clan to accumulate a sufficient amount of King-level karmic energy. Unfortunately, as each level of Rank 5 body cultivation involved consuming a Rank 5 demon beast, the amount of karmic energy needed for this was substantial.
That said, accumulating a large amount of King-level energy to pour into our body cultivators wasn’t as challenging as it might have been.
Most of the sects and several of the guilds were now producing King-level energy. We were generating enough of the stuff that, if concentrated, we could raise one or two people all the way from Peak Lord to Peak King every year.
At the same time, after an initial surge, the demand for King-level energy for regular, energy cultivation was dropping off since most of our people lacked the talents and affinities required for high-level cultivation.
In the lower Ranks, we had gotten around this through the use of Essence Gathering Formations and memory orbs. For Rank 5, however, that wasn’t going to work. I had never heard anyone even suggest that karmic essence might exist, and paying the System to imbue even a single jade slip with the details of even a single Rank 5 cultivation technique would cost a trillion credits.
I was still able to pass out orbs containing my personal memories, but these were far less effective than System-produced orbs. The only orbs I had from the past, and the only orbs that I could produce, were ones that contained memories of the Core of Fellowship. To cultivate this technique successfully, a person didn’t have to have both a high affinity and a high level of talent, but they definitely needed one or the other.
Therefore, nearly everyone was forced to learn their Rank 5 techniques through books and scrolls. And since these were, by definition, people who had a mediocre level of talent for cultivation, this was a lengthy process.
All in all, this meant that with each year that passed, the rate at which our Martial Kings consumed karmic energy slowly decreased. Surprisingly, though, the speed at which our body cultivators were consuming energy was increasing.
No one in the first group of body cultivators to reach Peak Rank 4 faced any difficulties when breaking through to Rank 5. And after they did break through, the only thing that stopped them from advancing directly to the Peak of Rank 5 was our lack of King-level energy and Rank 5 demon beasts.
Even beyond this first group, most of our people found that advancing as a body cultivator was surprisingly easy. Unlike energy cultivation, body cultivation just… made sense to them.
Why? Was body cultivation simply easier? This was possible, but it seemed unlikely.
ShouLi, Liang, and others had developed an entirely new cultivation system from scratch.
When I first met Liang, he hadn’t even been able to so much as understand a single word in a Rank 1 Low-Yellow cultivation technique. With the help of memory orbs, a bounty of essence, and a System-purchased improvement to his cultivation talent, he had been able to advance to Martial Emperor, but it had still been a struggle. How had such a boy been able to advance to Rank 5 of body cultivation so easily?
Most of the people in the Su Clan, Liang included, had never been able to understand what their blessings did. For the most part, they were treated as never having been blessed at all. But… What if their blessings were a boost to their comprehension of body cultivation?
Knowing what I did about the Earthly Dao, this wouldn’t surprise me.
Still, whether this was all a part of the Earthly Dao’s plans or not, it wouldn’t change what I needed to do. If I wanted to reach Martial Sovereign without selling my soul to a group of evil cultivators, I could only keep pressing forward.
Once TongBin achieved Peak Rank 5 of fire body cultivation, I took him back down to the cavern beneath Dragon Gate, and he destroyed the third ring of the formation.
Like always, this caused a minor earthquake. When it was over, we returned to the surface and headed to the elders’ meeting hall in the back of the Su Clan’s palace complex. Once there, I pulled ShouLi and the rest of the leadership council out of my inner world.
I smiled at everyone. “How does it feel to finally be free?”
This story has been stolen from . If you read it on Amazon, please report it
NiangBa gave an exaggerated sigh. “Ancestor, please, don’t do that to us again. I know that you were only trying to protect us, but six decades…”
Off to the side, GuiMing grunted. “At least you got to go out on trips to harvest essence.”
GuiAi slapped him on the back of the head. “At least you’re an earth cultivator. You don’t know what it was like in there for the rest of us. Six decades without even being able to replenish our qi…”
ShouLi waved a hand. “We can talk about this later. Right now, we need to discuss the situation in front of us.”
Nodding in agreement, everyone took their seat.
ShouLi cleared her throat. “For now, only Dragon Gate is open to us. If you try to go beyond the kingdom’s boundaries, the formation covering the Wastes will stop you. After a long discussion with the Ancestor, we’ve decided it needs to remain this way, at least for now.”
GuiMing winced as if struck. “How long?”
ShouLi shook her head. “I don’t know. Decades, possibly longer.”
This caused several people to grimace, so ShouLi gestured for me to explain.
“We have two problems: the Sovereign Clans and the Nine Rivers Sect. Until we erase the final ring, the Sovereigns themselves shouldn’t pose much of a threat, but we don’t know how powerful the clans under their control might be. More importantly, we
do
know that the Nine Rivers Sect’s Earth City is home to hundreds of Emperors and tens of thousands of Kings. Nearly all of them are old men and women who have had centuries to master their skills. If the sect releases a mission to attack us, we will quickly be overwhelmed.”
This statement made the elderly mortal councilwoman next to GuiAi knead her hands in worry. “Ancestor… you’ve… taken down our protections against Kings, right? What if they don’t wait? What if they invade now?”Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
I shook my head. “It’s possible, but it’s unlikely. If they were going to strike, they would have done so the moment we broke the formation in the Twin Mountains Sect. Since they haven’t done so, they are likely waiting for us to open the Wastes to Emperors. Though, they might wait until the formation is down entirely.”
What I didn’t say was that this was my interpretation of Emperor Li’s message to me. By breaking the third ring of Dragon Gate’s formation, I could ascend to Peak Emperor. Now, we needed to bide our time and build our strength before proceeding any further.
I looked at Mo. “I want the entirety of Dragon Gate Kingdom surrounded in Rank 6 formations. With the low qi density in the Wastes, providing power to such a formation will be difficult, so we also need to look into creating some form of large-scale qi storage. In the interim, we can rely on spirit stones.”
I turned to Liang. “Over the last few decades, we’ve been pulling in everyone we can from everywhere on the continent. The sects are likely teeming with spies and traitors. Don’t rush to purge them, but we will need enforcers capable of taking people down before they can cause any trouble.”
I look at GuiAi and GuiMing. “Now that everyone can leave the world orb, I’m going to look at doing a bit of remodeling in there. However, this time, I don’t want us to abandon it. If possible, I want Chang’an to become a true city that permanently houses enough people to generate karmic energy.”
“Ancestor…” GuiAi looked like she wanted to weep. The thought of housing over a hundred thousand people within a space of only two square kilometers was nearly too much for her to bear.
I waved away her concern. “Just see what’s feasible. A true city is the goal, but if that’s not possible without more space, then it’s not possible.”
After this, we talked through a few smaller objectives, but the main point of each of them was the same. We needed to find new ways to increase our strength. For ShouLi and NiangBa, this meant improving their body cultivation techniques. For GuiAi and GuiMing, it meant increasing the rate at which we generated karmic energy. For Mo and RuLan, it meant crafting more Rank 6 items. For me, it meant increasing my personal strength so that I would be able to stand against the Sovereigns.
Once this meeting was over, I secluded myself away in a remote corner of the Su Clan’s Hall of Ancestral Worship and faded from public view.
I was certain that as soon as the final rings of the Wastes’ formations were broken, the Sovereigns would invade. At that point, we would have Peak Rank 6 body cultivators, and there was no doubt in my mind that the Sovereigns would do everything in their power to learn what we knew.
Why hadn’t they invaded already? It might have been because they were worried about walking into a trap, but it was likely because they wanted to see how far we could advance first. Once we reached Peak Rank 6 and were able to break the final rings of formations, the Sovereigns would swoop in and claim the rewards for all of our hard work for themselves.
However, I had no intention of making a wedding dress for someone else. I
intended
to break through to Sovereign, fight them off, and then raid their treasuries.
To do that, though, I needed the ability to fight against four—possibly five—cultivators whose levels might be as high as Peak Sovereign. This was a nearly impossible task. To have even the slightest hope of success, I needed to be
far
more powerful than ever before.
Within the Wastes, I couldn’t ascend past Peak Emperor, so if I wanted to become stronger, there was only one path open to me.
“System, increase my comprehension of body cultivation by 100 billion credits.”
Purchase confirmed. 154,998,662,935 credits remaining.
I took out all of the notes that I had compiled on the various techniques and refinements that ShouLi and the others had produced.
I needed to ascend to the Peak of Rank 6 before the final ring of the formation was removed, but there was no need to rush. I could take things one step at a time.
Using my analysis ability, I examined ShouLi’s Rank 1 technique.
Skin Refining, Low-Yellow Rank 1 Body Cultivation Technique (Broken), Wu (Any Element), Effects: Makes one more obsessed with body cultivation. Makes one more obsessed with growing stronger.
Seeing this, I nodded. It made sense. This cultivation technique had been inscribed into ShouLi by the Earthly Dao. And what did the Earthly Dao want? It wanted people to grow stronger, and, based on everything I had seen in the Wastes, it wanted people to explore body cultivation.
I, however, had no interest in inheriting these obsessions. So, I began modifying, refining, and enhancing this technique one step at a time.

chapters.title: Chapter 310 – Life 76, Age 72, Martial King Peak
chapters.content:
Without actively cultivating it myself, understanding ShouLi’s technique well enough to modify it was rather tricky. However, since I was nowhere near ready to give up on this life, I didn’t want to cultivate a technique with severe potential side effects. I needed to find some way to improve it with only my notes and observations of others to guide me.
This was a nearly impossible task. The only thing that even made it somewhat feasible was that I could use my analysis ability to check the effects of each change I made as I made them.
Re-examining the technique, I made note of a few specifics.
Low-Yellow Rank 1 Body Cultivation Technique (Broken), Wu (Any Element)
‘Broken.’ Why was the technique broken? This was likely because it lacked any form of wu filter, and without such a filter, it could only be cultivated in a specially prepared environment.
If I could only change one thing about this technique, it would be adding in the proper filters. However, I had good reason to believe that there was currently no viable way to make such a change. In the past, when I had tried to purchase wu filters from the System, I was told the price was ‘1 shard.’ This suggested that no such filters existed anywhere in this entire world.
A more promising direction of research was searching for a way to improve the technique beyond Low-Yellow. However, based on what I knew about rankings for qi cultivation techniques, I doubted that there would be much I could do to shift this categorization without including proper filters.
Finally, there was the information about what type of energy this technique used.
Wu (Any Element)
At first, this appeared to be nothing more than basic, obvious information. Most of the people in my clan had used this technique to cultivate earth wu since that was the only type of energy that they had been able to gather within my inner world. However, Liang had used it to cultivate lightning wu while in the sect, and younger cultivators, like TongBin, the ones who weren’t trapped within my inner world, had used it to cultivate whatever elements they chose.
What was interesting, though, was that, from what my analysis ability was telling me, any element could be used with this technique
without
changing its mental effects.
I had come to believe that the mental effects of a technique were the result of a person’s body attuning itself to specific Laws. If that were true, what did it tell me?
This technique didn’t attune a person’s body to elemental Laws. It attuned the body to Laws of Wu. In a way, this was similar to the Rank 4 and 5 techniques that I had been studying. Those were focused on Laws of Karma.
This idea seemed like it might lead me to a goldmine, since if this technique could be attuned to Laws of Wu, then others should be able to connect to Laws of Qi. Unfortunately, though, without more examples to draw from, I wouldn’t even know what Laws those were or what they could do.
I could only note this bit of information down for future research and refocus on the task at hand.
While playing around with potential Laws of Wu might be nice, that wasn’t my immediate goal. Instead, I wanted to replace the Laws in the technique with Laws of Metal. Specifically, I wanted to replace them with the Laws that I had used in my qi cultivation technique. While this might make the mental effects of both techniques more powerful, it felt like the right thing to do.
For my qi technique, the Laws that I had focused on were related to swiftness, sharpness, and integrity, forming the Writ of Quicksilver.
Writ of Quicksilver, Peak-Earth Rank 1 Cultivation Technique, Metal Qi, Effects: Increases one’s integrity. Makes one more likely to react without thinking.
However, while being able to react without thinking was ideal in
certain
situations, it wasn’t an effect that I would want to be subjected to continuously. Instead, I wanted to use the swiftness Laws to help me move faster. The inevitable mental effects could come from other Laws.The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
How exactly could I translate the Laws from the Writ of Quicksilver into a body cultivation technique, though? With ShouLi’s technique, which flows of energy were related to Laws and which were just a natural result of cultivating one’s body? Did that question even make logical sense?
Without more techniques to work from, this task seemed impossible.
So, I turned to the System for assistance.
“System, how much would it cost to modify the effects of ShouLi’s body cultivation technique so that it only increases a person’s integrity?”
Calculating… Cost 1 shard.
My cheek twitched at that answer, but it wasn’t entirely unexpected.
“How much to change the
primary
mental effect to one that increases a person’s integrity?”
Calculating… Cost 1,000,000 credits.
“Purchase.”
Purchase confirmed. 154,997,662,935 credits remaining.
I focused on the new technique that appeared in my mental library and examined it.
Enjoying the story? Show your support by reading it on the official site.
Drill of Probity, Low-Yellow Rank 1 Body Cultivation Technique (Broken), Metal Wu, Effects: Increases one’s integrity. Makes one more obsessed with growing stronger.
This technique was still far from ideal, but it gave me a starting point.
Over the next year, I studied the Drill of Probity in extensive detail.
By comparing it to both ShouLi’s Skin Refining technique and a variety of random Low-Yellow qi techniques that focused on integrity-based Laws, I was able to nail down the exact energy pathways that were causing these Laws to be manifested.
Once I had that, I took out several Low-Yellow qi techniques based around swiftness Laws and attempted to construct a brand-new technique based on them. This took a bit of trial and error, but, eventually, I was able to make it work.
Drill of Impulsivity, Low-Yellow Rank 1 Body Cultivation Technique (Broken), Metal Wu, Effects: Makes one more likely to react without thinking. Makes one more obsessed with growing stronger.
After that, constructing another technique around sharpness Laws wasn’t too difficult.
This gave me three new Low-Yellow Rank 1 body cultivation techniques, but none of them were what I was looking for. The Drill of Probity wasn’t terrible, and I could use it if necessary, but I was hoping to construct something better.
Turning my attention to Low-Profound qi techniques, I began trying to incorporate their Laws into my body cultivation techniques.
After another three years of hard work, I had little to show for my efforts. None of the ‘techniques’ I made would even register with my analysis ability, and I didn’t know what I was doing wrong. I had to be making some kind of basic error, but what?
The only way that I could get to the bottom of this was by testing it. I
wanted
to test it on myself—I hated the idea of having someone else ruin their future just to protect me—but I knew that was a bad idea. I was aiming to reach Martial Sovereign in this life, and experimenting with failed techniques was a good way to cut my future short.
So, I had ShouLi post a mission targeted at a very select group of cultivators. If any of them were willing to help me with my experiments, they would be amply rewarded.
Almost immediately, two old men appeared in my study. I gave them a martial salute and bowed my head to them. “Grand Elder TaiZu, Ancestor HongYi, greetings.”
HongYi clasped his hands together and bowed his head as if asking for forgiveness. “No, no, Ancestor Fang. Please, do not call me that. I am merely one of the clan’s inner disciples. If not for your and Elder ShouLi’s magnanimity in granting me karmic energy, I would be dead by now.”
Abashed, TaiZu gave me a deep bow. “Ancestor Fang, I am but a lowly outer disciple. Thank you for providing me with karmic energy.”
The immense shift in the behavior of these two took me by surprise. Gratitude was one thing, but this seemed a bit much. What had they experienced over the past few decades?
I waved away their thanks and took out a technique scroll for each of them. “This is why I brought you here. These are
supposed
to be Low-Profound Rank 1 body cultivation techniques. They are failures, but I don’t know why. I need someone to cultivate them so that I can study them in more detail.”
I looked both men dead in the eye. “I do not know what cultivating these techniques will do to you. It may cause you immense pain, it may cripple you, or… it may kill you. Are you certain that you are willing to test them for me?”
HongYi took a deep breath and nodded. “Yes, Ancestor Fang. Without your assistance, I would be dead by now. I only hope…”
Knowing his meaning, I took out two memory orbs and placed one in front of each man. “Do not worry. As long as you assist me, I will treat you fairly.”
Both men bowed excitedly, picked up their orbs, and injected their memories into them.
It took the old men several days to understand even the basics of the techniques that I had given them, and once they started trying to cultivate them, they ran into countless problems.
I switched them to the Low-Yellow technique that I had purchased from the System, but the result was the same. Their bodies just did not want to absorb any wu.
With this being the case, my plan for using these old guys as training dummies might have been doomed to failure, but I wasn’t willing to give up quite yet. I was asking them to cultivate metal techniques, and neither of them had any affinity for metal. I
could
try sending them to a Metal Essence Gathering Formation for a bit to check if a decent affinity would help, but I didn’t. I had an even better idea.
They didn’t have an affinity for metal. So, with my extremely high affinity, shouldn’t I be able to control metal wu even after it entered their bodies?
“Actually…” I began to get excited as I looked at my two test subjects. “Elder HongYi, please, return to the formation.”
HongYi’s head drooped, but he did as I requested. After spending over a week in the formation with nothing to show for it, he had begun to look depressed, but I didn’t let that dampen my enthusiasm.
Once he was seated in the lotus position, I sat down next to him.
“I am going to guide the wu through your body. This will be just like how I helped you break through to Martial Lord. Relax your mind, and don’t resist.”
He ducked his head. “Yes, Ancestor.”
I placed my right hand on the small of his back and used my left hand to cover his right wrist. Then, I pulled wu from the environment and shoved it into both parts of his body at the same time.
The wu in his lower back spread through his torso, and the wu in his wrist spread through his arm.
While keeping my right hand on his back, I moved my left hand to his left wrist and repeated this process. After infusing his arms with energy, I moved to his legs and, finally, to his head.
The wu that I had injected into HongYi’s body was now his, but in a way, it was also still mine, so I retained an elevated level of control over it.
Once his entire body was filled with this initial portion of wu, I began circulating it through his skin in the manner dictated by the Profound-Rank technique that I had created.
As I did, I felt several areas of increased resistance. Focusing on them, I shifted the flow of wu and redirected it.
When everything looked good, I pulled in more wu from the environment and injected it into HongYi's body. Again, I felt areas of increased resistance, so I modified the technique to work around them.
After this third round, I stopped for the day and allowed his body to adjust.
From then on, I paid HongYi a visit each and every day. I would inject him with energy, and as it moved through his body, I would shift it to fix any problems. Then, I would leave him alone to acclimate.
After a full month of this routine, HongYi finally broke through, and I received the notification that I had been waiting for.
System Alert: A novel cultivation technique has been created. Please name your technique.
“Drill of Swift Probity.”
The Drill of Swift Probity. Rating: Low-Profound Rank 1 Metal Body Cultivation Technique. Would you like to submit this technique to the Dao?
“Yes.”
Submission successful. Contribution confirmed. Calculating… Reward: 50% discount for the next purchase below 5,000 credits.
Note: Profound Rank 1 body cultivation techniques will no longer qualify you for further discounts.
Then, I received the enlightenment that I had been hoping for. Once it was done, I examined my new technique.
Drill of Swift Probity, Low-Profound Rank 1 Body Cultivation Technique (Broken), Metal Wu, Effects: Increases one’s integrity. Makes one more obsessed with growing stronger.
It was good, but I knew that I could do better.

chapters.title: Chapter 311 – Life 76, Age 81, Martial King Peak
chapters.content:
After using HongYi to develop a solid Low-Profound body cultivation technique, I returned to my secluded research and worked on finding ways to incorporate Earth-Rank Laws into it. When I had a partial technique that seemed like it might work, I sought out TaiZu and performed another round of experiments.
This resulted in him howling in pain a few times, but he never asked me to stop. He just wanted me to finish my work as quickly as possible.
I tried to comply with this request, but perfecting my new technique was challenging. Each day, I would find him, fiddle around with his energy flows, and then leave him to recover. It wasn’t until after nearly an entire year of this that I finally accomplished my goal.
Regimen of Quicksilver, Low-Earth Rank 1 Body Cultivation Technique (Broken), Metal Wu, Effects: Increases one’s integrity. Allows one to think more clearly. Makes one more obsessed with growing stronger.
Nothing I tried had ever been able to change the ‘broken’ classification, so I was convinced that it was due to a lack of wu filters. While not ideal, this was something that I could work with. So, after receiving my enlightenment and discount—50% off my next purchase under 50,000 credits—I returned to my seclusion and cultivated my body for the first time.
With qi cultivation, I usually never
felt
anything. A couple of the more unusual Earth-Rank techniques that I had practiced caused certain sensations because of the way they combined elements, but the processes involved in pulling in energy, piercing my acupoints, and building meridians had never really caused any physical sensations in and of themselves.
Body cultivation was different. As I pulled in wu and pushed it through my skin, I felt as if small worms were wriggling their way through my body. This wasn’t painful, not exactly, but it was… disturbing.
After establishing an initial set of pathways, circulating wu through my body caused my skin to seize up and contract.
Then, as my skin tightened around my muscles, a black, foul-smelling oil was forced out of my pores. At first, there were only a few drops, but after only a few minutes, these few drops turned into a thick layer.
Finally, just as my skin was reaching the point where I thought that it might tear itself apart, it relaxed. I had broken through to level 1 of Rank 1 of body cultivation.
After stabilizing my new realm, I exited my room and headed directly to the bath. It took me several rounds of vigorous scrubbing to remove the oily impurities that I had expelled, but, thankfully, no matter how hard I scrubbed, the brush didn’t cause any damage to my skin.
Once this oily residue was completely removed, I was able to see that my breakthrough had caused my skin to turn several shades lighter. And, under the right kind of lighting, it produced an almost metallic shimmer.
Researching Rank 1 of body cultivation had taken me a bit longer than I had expected, and during this time, while I had continued my monthly routine of pulling people into and out of my inner world, I hadn’t paid much attention to other goings-on in the world. So, when I exited my cultivation chamber, the first thing I did was catch up on everything that I had missed. Thankfully, it seemed like my clan had been thriving in my absence.
Dragon Gate Kingdom and the surrounding eight sects had all become large enough that they were producing a steady flow of King-level karmic energy. In fact, the sects were even starting to see problems with
over
population.
Each year, thousands of hopefuls from around the continent would travel to the Wastes to join our sects. Then, after joining, almost no one would leave.
At first, when we were trying to grow our population, this had been a good thing. However, after several decades, the sects were starting to have an overabundance of Grandmasters. They all stayed on in the hope that they might one day be given access to karmic energy, but with only 10 cities per sect generating energy, and with a large portion of that energy being reserved for members of the Su Clan, most of those hopes were in vain.
Eventually, ShouLi was forced to implement a new rule. After the age of 50, Grandmasters who were not being considered for leadership positions had to leave. They could return home, or they could head to the Nine Rivers Sect, but they couldn’t stay in the Wastes.
Implementing this policy meant that, each year, thousands of Grandmasters were sent back to wherever they had come from. At first, this worked. With so many Grandmasters leaving the sects, their populations stabilized and even started to decline. However, after only a few years of this, a new problem emerged. The sects were being flooded with new recruits.
Originally, the Rulers of the places we were recruiting from had been concerned about us stealing away their citizens. They needed a strong population base as much as we did, so seeing their people run away to some sect had made them worried.
However, upon seeing that we were willing to raise these children to Peak Grandmaster, teach them a profession, and then just… send them away, these Rulers immediately wanted to use us for their own benefit. Having seen that we never turned anyone away due to low talent or affinities, they began shipping every child they could to our sects. In response, ShouLi and the Sect Masters had to implement another round of new policies to weed out poor performers and stabilize our population base.
Stolen content warning: this content belongs on . Report any occurrences.
One interesting knock-on effect of this was a shift in the way people viewed refiners.
In the past, refiners had been suppressed. While every Emperor wanted an armory filled with refined items, they had no desire to see such an armory in the hands of their rivals. So, they assassinated each other’s refiners, and when they found a refiner in their own lands, they kidnapped them and forced them to make items in secret.
With the establishment of the Rosehill Sect, though, things changed.
After only a couple of years, the sect was pumping out Rank 1 items at a prodigious pace. And, as we had no need for so many low-quality weapons, most of them were sold off to traveling merchants.
After less than a decade, the sect began selling off Rank 2 items.
After less than three decades, the same was true of Rank 3 items.
At first, bandit groups, likely under the control of various Emperors and Sovereigns, tried to prevent these weapons from leaving the Wastes. As time went on, though, this proved to be a losing strategy. We were simply making too many weapons.
So, once the Rosehill Sect began expelling its older, more experienced Grandmasters, various powers showed up to vie for a chance to recruit them. This was partially to stay ahead of their rivals, but it was also because they realized something important: such a large sect had to possess a number of Lords and Kings. Since we were not selling off any Rank 4 or 5 items, if they wanted to be able to fight against us in the future, they would need Artifact Lords and Kings of their own.
Even with these changes, with each year that passed, worry about the ‘refiner situation’ grew.
Then, in the far north of the continent, in an insignificant subsidiary kingdom of the Empire of Eternal Winter, a new organization took root.
According to reports, several decades earlier, a group of bandits had attacked this kingdom. During this attack, one of the kingdom’s princes had been killed, and one of its princesses had been kidnapped. This princess, Shi YuHua, was then sold off to the Rosehill Sect. At that time, she was only 9 years old.
After arriving in the sect, she was treated as a slave and was forced to do all kinds of menial tasks. If she didn’t do a good enough job, she was whipped. If she spent too much time on a task, she was whipped. And sometimes, she was whipped just because her taskmasters felt bored.
However, upon turning 16, YuHua was blessed with the ability to shape metal with only a thought. This allowed her to eventually rise up to a position of importance in the sect, but she never forgot the humiliation that she had endured as a child.
In time, she gained the sect’s trust, ascended to Peak Lord, and learned the skills of a top-level Artifact Lord. She even learned a few of the secrets that were reserved for the sect’s Kings.
Then, she escaped.
After sneaking out of the sect at night, YuHua hid in a merchant caravan and stealthily made her way back to the Empire of Eternal Winter.
Once there, she formed a new guild, the Guild of Refiners. Its sole goal was to destroy the Rosehill Sect at any cost. With this continent’s Rulers now convinced that they needed to start arming themselves with better weaponry, and with this new guild being the only open source of Rank 4 weapons and armor, countless Kings and Lords rushed to support it.
Did all of these Rulers actually believe the story that we had concocted for YuHua? Probably not, but that didn’t change the fact that they needed the guild’s weaponry.
With everything progressing smoothly, I paid my yearly visit to ShouLi. As the Emperor of the Wastes, she had harvested a substantial amount of karmic energy, and it needed to be moved from her to the people who had paid for it. This time, however, I retained a large portion of the energy for my own use—specifically, the portion of the energy that had been generated by members of the Su Clan.
Then, I returned to my cultivation chamber and got to work on designing a new Rank 6 cultivation technique.
In my last life, I had found creating a Rank 6 core to be rather challenging. Unlike Ranks 4 and 5, I hadn’t felt much of a connection to the karmic energy, and my understanding of how to properly shape it had been limited.
This time, after infusing my entire core with Emperor-level energy, I felt… something. Due to my lack of a Rank 4 karmic energy affinity, this feeling wasn’t as clear as it had been at the lower Ranks, but with my greater understanding of the principles of refining, I was able to sense… something.
Using these impulses as a guide, I constructed the best core possible. It wasn’t perfect, but with the temporary affinity boost that I had purchased previously, I was able to shape the Emperor-level energy nearly as well as I could shape King-level energy.
Once the work on my core was complete, I did my best to design a new weave of qi and karmic energy for destroying the Emperor-level chains. Unfortunately, without enough credits to further upgrade my technique analysis ability, I couldn’t check to see how good a job I had done. I could only do my best to replicate what I had done for Ranks 4 and 5.
When it was finally as good as it was going to get, I filled my core with qi, opened a hole in the world, and broke through to Martial Emperor.
As soon as this breakthrough was complete, I recorded everything in a memory orb. Then, I wrote it down in a technique manual. Both the orb and the book had their share of flaws, but this was undoubtedly the best Rank 6 cultivation technique that I had ever possessed.
After this breakthrough, I hoarded any karmic energy generated by members of the Su Clan and propelled myself to Peak Emperor at the fastest possible speed. However, as ‘the fastest possible speed’ was measured in decades, I returned to my research while I waited for the energy I needed to accumulate.
Using HongYi and TaiZu as my guinea pigs, I researched first Rank 2 and then Rank 3 body cultivation techniques.
As ShouLi had already discovered, Ranks 2 and 3 were not entirely dissimilar to Rank 1. So, with the enlightenment that I had received, it wasn’t too difficult to combine my Rank 1 techniques with what she had already figured out for Ranks 2 and 3.
By creating both a Profound- and an Earth-Rank technique at both Ranks, I received four more enlightenments and four more discounts. Even the greatest of these discounts was only for 50% off my next purchase under 500 million credits, but I wouldn’t turn my nose up at them.
Having ascended to Peak Emperor, and having reached Peak Rank 3 of body cultivation, I was more powerful than I had ever been, but was I powerful enough to face a Sovereign?
No. Not on my own.
By combining all of my skills and abilities, I might be able to fight a Sovereign in one-on-one combat, but why would they give me such an opportunity? Even if they did at first, if I started winning, they would come at me with the full might of their armies.
How powerful was a Sovereign Clan? How many Emperors did they have? How many could they pull from other empires around the Wastes? The Jiu Clan was in control of the Nine Rivers Sect. How many of the sect’s Emperors would they be able to throw at us?
The moment we broke the barrier that was keeping the Sovereigns out of the Wastes, they would come for us. So, if I wanted to gain the time I needed to ascend in peace, then I needed help. I needed a clan.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet

chapters.title: Chapter 312 – Life 76, Age 112, Martial Emperor Peak
chapters.content:
By the time I was able to reach Peak Emperor, my body was only eight years away from entering stagnation. I wanted to rush to break through to Sovereign before that happened, but I knew that doing so would put everyone in my clan at risk.
More to the point, even if I protected everyone by storing them in my inner world, attempting to ascend too early could lead to the destruction of everything that we had built over this past century. With everything we had learned, rebuilding would be significantly easier, but I wasn’t sure how the people in my clan would handle that. I doubted anyone would be thrilled to find out that the life they had spent 100 years building had been destroyed because the ‘ancestor’ decided to rush his cultivation.
After a bit of soul-searching, I calmed down. Entering stagnation wouldn’t be so bad. I would still be able to progress. Even if I entered the early stages of calcification, I could still try to ascend. It might be more difficult, but it should still be possible.
Besides, what had Emperor Li told me? “As for the final breakthrough to Sovereign, make sure that you are fully prepared.” Without even reaching Rank 6 of body cultivation, how could I dare to consider myself “fully prepared?”
I needed to wait. There was still so much more I needed to do.
Ever since we broke the third ring of formation beneath Dragon Gate, ShouLi had been the unannounced Emperor of the Wastes. The head of the Dragon Gate Kingdom, the Sect Masters, the city lords, and the upper-level members of our clan all knew of her position, but it was not common knowledge among the wider populace.
We had done this in order to achieve two different, but related, goals. With any luck, not announcing ShouLi’s position might lead outsiders to think that we were still limited to King-level karma. But, even if they did figure out that we were an official empire, by leaving ShouLi in charge, they might think that she was our only Emperor.
In any case, because ShouLi was our
official
Emperor, she was the one who received all of our Emperor-level karma, so I had to make yearly trips to distribute it to the people who had purchased it. During the first such trip after I advanced to Rank 3 of body cultivation, we sat down to talk about our plans for the future.
“ShouLi, for the next several years, I need to reserve about a tenth of the karma you are receiving for my own use. All of it will be from the pool of Su Clan karma.”
This tenth was the karmic energy being generated by people connected to me through both body and soul. From what Emperor Li had told me at the Summit of the Nine Rivers Sect, all I needed to do to advance to Sovereign was infuse my core with copious amounts of this energy. Even though I had no plans to rush my breakthrough, since this energy was rather scarce, I figured that it would be best to go ahead and start accumulating it.
ShouLi bowed her head. “Yes, Ancestor. I will make the arrangements.”
I walked over to where ShouLi had a map of the Wastes laid out across a large table.
“How have things been going with the clan? Is everything still running smoothly?”
ShouLi’s movements hitched slightly as she moved over to stand next to me. “For the most part…”
I raised an eyebrow at that but allowed her to continue without interruption.
“Ancestor, there are a few things we have been considering, and it would be good if we could get your input on them.” She reached into her storage bag, pulled out a map of the entire continent, and laid it atop the map of the Wastes. “In the north, Shi YuHua has done an excellent job of growing the Guild of Refiners. For karmic purposes, it already registers as an official kingdom. However, it still can’t compare to the older guilds.”
She made a wide, sweeping gesture to the set of kingdoms and empires marked with a red pill furnace. “Chang’s Guild of Alchemists is more than large enough to become an independent empire. The guilds for the formation specialists, beast tamers, herbalists, and talisman artists are a bit smaller, but they are nearly at the same point. The only guild that
hasn’t
seen its share of success is the Guild of Illusionists, and that’s because we don’t have the right Essence Gathering Formations. Though, from reports, the Zhuge Clan’s suppression is also a contributing factor.”
I nodded, impressed. It had been a while since I had checked in on the guilds, and I hadn’t expected their progress to be so swift.
Realizing the cause of this rapid expansion, I smiled. “This is because the Sovereigns are trying to suppress us here in the Wastes, isn’t it?”
ShouLi nodded. “Yes. They are encouraging Lords to send their children to the guilds so that they
won’t
send them to the sects.”
At the start of this life, Yan had gone back to the Zhuge Clan, and with his blessing, he could have easily risen to become the clan’s chief strategist. Was he behind this? If so, it should have been good for us. Why did ShouLi look so worried?
“Will this be a problem?”
ShouLi hesitated but shook her head. “Not… exactly. The population base of the sects is solid at this point. Even with no outside recruits, they won’t have any problem maintaining their status as kingdoms.”
I looked at her and furrowed my brow. “What’s wrong?”
She sighed and waved a hand at the map again. “Aside from the Guild of Illusionists, all of the guilds are either already large enough to be empires, or they soon will be. Keeping them within the umbrella of the Empire of the Wastes is just limiting their potential for karmic energy generation.”
I nodded. “This is what we expected, right? Branch them off. That way, we’ll have multiple, distinct empires.”
Help support creative writers by finding and reading their stories on the original site.
“Yes… but… If we do that, we run into a problem. The Empire of the Wastes isn’t big enough. We only have 8 kingdoms here. If we include the Guild of Illusionists, that’s 9. We need 10 to qualify as an official empire and generate Emperor-level karmic energy. Without the other guilds, we’ll be one kingdom short.”
ShouLi was acting rather nervous, but I wasn’t sure why. Even though the Wastes only contained 8 official kingdoms, our population was more than sufficient to spawn off a ninth. Arranging everything and drawing up official borders might be troublesome, but it shouldn’t be too difficult.
I looked her in the eye. “What do you want to say?”
She winced. Then, she put away the map of the continent and gestured to the map of the Wastes.
“Dragon Gate Kingdom is in the center. More than anything, it serves as our base. There are sects in all four cardinal directions and three of the ordinal directions. These sects serve as training centers for seven of the eight professions. Looking at the map, we can see that there is still one area relatively open, the southwest. The leadership council and I have been discussing whether or not we should construct a new sect there. If we do…”
I closed my eyes, finally understanding her meaning.
If we were going to spin most of the guilds off to form their own empires, we needed to start working on forming a new kingdom. While we
could
just throw up a few random cities and call it a day, that likely wasn’t the best option.
We already had sects for seven out of the eight professions. Wouldn’t it make the most sense if our final kingdom were a sect for the final profession?
I’d had a strong aversion to wind cultivators and gu keepers ever since I had first met them. This was partially a normal reaction to the fact that gu keepers were mostly shunned by society, but it was mostly due to me not wanting my soul to be infested with demonic insects.
That said, I could admit that every profession had its evil side. Beast tamers would slaughter cultivators and feed the bodies to their companions in the hope of raising them to Rank 4. Alchemists could concoct countless different pills to poison both a person’s body and soul. And, while I had never actually seen it happen, I had read accounts of formation specialists who learned to use human remains to create especially powerful formations.
So, while my introduction to gu keeper hadn’t been the best, I could still admit that they were not somehow inherently, uniquely more evil than any other professionals.
Still, even putting that aside… Was making a sect for gu keepers the right move? There were a few problems with the idea.
Most importantly, no one in the clan knew anything about gu keeping. I didn’t even have any books on the topic in my mental library. Outside of the Nine Rivers Sect, gu keeping was shunned, so finding any information on the topic was difficult. Within the Nine Rivers Sect, manuals on gu keeping were kept on the Wind Peak, and I had never even considered visiting that place. Even when compared to the other peaks, the Wind Peak felt supremely dangerous. How was I supposed to set up a sect without any information?
Still… I did have ways to acquire the information we needed, but even if I did, we didn’t have any gu eggs. Well, I did still have
one
tucked away in my inner world, but I couldn’t exactly start a sect with only a single soul gu egg.
Also, there was the problem of affinities. I didn’t have a diagram for a Wind Essence Gathering Formation, so I couldn’t raise people’s wind affinities, and since wind was a secondary element, people’s wind affinities were naturally lower than affinities for the primary elements. This meant that only a minority of the people who joined this potential gu keeping sect would even have a chance of reaching Grandmaster.
Still…
As I walked aimlessly through the streets of Dragon Gate City, I pulled out three jade slips.
“System, imbue one of these slips with all of the knowledge that would be expected from one of this continent’s top-level Gu Disciples. Imbue another with similar knowledge for a Gu Master, and imbue the third with the knowledge of a Gu Grandmaster.”
Purchase confirmed. Cost 10,101,000,000 credits. 144,896,662,935 credits remaining.
I juggled the three small jade slips in my hand for a moment.
Should I absorb their knowledge? I didn’t like the idea of getting my crafting knowledge from the System. I wanted to learn it myself. So, if this were just a matter of learning the art of gu keeping, it wouldn’t even be a question. But this was also about the safety of my people. Was it right to release the information contained in these slips without knowing what they contained?
Making up my mind, I inserted my qi into the Rank 1 slip and absorbed the memories contained within. Then, I carefully sorted through everything and checked for any potential dangers.
Once I was done, I sent a wave of qi into my soul and crushed the orb of energy that contained the jade slip's information. This caused me to completely forget everything that I had just learned about gu keeping, but I retained a certainty that my clan could deal with any difficulties that the knowledge in that slip might cause.
After this, I repeated my actions with the slips for Ranks 2 and 3.
As I considered what I had learned, my legs took me to one of the minor administration buildings that dealt with the disposition of apartments in the city’s western quadrant.
I breezed past a security guard who tried to block my path and made my way up to the second floor.
There, I found the desk where a young-looking woman was hard at work.
“Hello, Mei. Let’s talk.”
After taking Mei to a tea house, I showed her the three jade slips and told her my intentions.
She stared at me, mouth agape. “You… You want me to start a sect for gu keepers?”
I nodded seriously. “Yes. The clan will provide you with all the support you need to get started. These slips contain a lot of what you need to know, but I don’t want you just handing them out to people. The information needs to be written down in books. We will also need to get supplementary technique manuals, and we will need to find a source of gu eggs.”
“An… Ancestor Su…” Mei was visibly struggling with my sudden request. “I don’t think…”
“Pei LiMei.” I looked at her and gave my best impression of Emperor Li’s granite expression. “I have investigated your background. Daughter of the Pei Clan, direct descendant of the Emperor of the Tranquil Springs. You were raised to be a Ruler. You know what it involves. Your blessing may have gotten you kicked out of your clan, but I am certain that you haven’t forgotten all the lessons you learned as a child.”
She dropped her head.
“As a 113-year-old Lord, you have already entered stagnation. If you are willing to become the Sect Master, I will immediately raise you to King. If you do a good enough job, you will have the chance to ascend to Emperor one day. However, all you need to do is your best. If there are any problems, the clan will deal with them.”
I could see Mei struggling. After leaving the Blue Wind Pavilion, she had spent almost all her time studying soul cultivation to get her blessing under control. At several points, she had said she wanted to contribute more to the clan, but nothing had worked out. Now, I was giving her a huge opportunity to do just that, but after years of failure, she was struggling with the weight of it.
I softened my expression as best I could. “Just give it a shot. If it doesn’t work out, it doesn’t work out.”
Mei dipped her head. “Yes… Ancestor Su.”
After setting Mei up with the three jade slips and a large collection of wind cultivation techniques, I handed her off to ShouLi. I was still skeptical about the idea of a gu keeper sect, but if that was what my clan’s leadership thought was best, then I wouldn’t stand in the way.
I checked in on a few more people, but, eventually, I returned to the place I had spent the majority of this life, my spartan, windowless cultivation room in a remote corner of the Su Clan’s Hall of Ancestral Worship.
Once there, I began working on unraveling the secrets of ShouLi’s Rank 4 body cultivation technique.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt

chapters.title: Chapter 313 – Life 76, Age 140, Martial Emperor Peak
chapters.content:
Even after decades of research, I was only able to make minor improvements to ShouLi’s Rank 4 body cultivation technique. Everything I tried had only resulted in broken Low-Yellow techniques. Still, even though this rating hadn’t changed, I wasn’t entirely unhappy with my results.
Drill of Fellowship, Low-Yellow Rank 4 Body Cultivation Technique (Broken), Karmic Energy, Effects: Makes those connected by this technique feel an enhanced sense of community. Makes one more obsessed with growing stronger.
Aside from changing the technique’s primary mental effect, I had also found several ways to reduce the amount of karmic energy it needed, including a method to cultivate it without the need to consume the meat of Rank 4 beasts.
Unfortunately, the method I had devised was rather difficult. One needed to draw karmic energy out of their dantian, pull it through their acupoints—into their physical body, and then delicately weave it into their wu before absorbing it into their muscles. This was all rather tricky to accomplish, and manipulating karmic energy outside of one’s dantian was rather finicky in the best of circumstances.
Simply put, it was impossible to cultivate the Drill of Fellowship without a high affinity for karmic energy.
Did this mean that I had wasted the last 28 years of my life? Not exactly.
I considered the effects of both the Core of Fellowship and this new Drill of Fellowship to be extremely important for our plans going forward. By expelling people from the sects when they turned 50, we were essentially training up Peak Grandmasters and handing them over to our enemies. These techniques, however, would keep them connected to us by karma, making them less willing to act against us.
So, while developing the Drill of Fellowship had taken longer than I would have liked, I was happy with the result.
That said, the issue of needing an affinity for karmic energy couldn’t just be ignored. While I was able to assist a person in cultivating the technique by taking direct control of their energy, I didn’t want to have to assist
everyone
at
every
stage of Ruler Tier body cultivation. At the same time, I had no way to raise the karmic affinity of everyone in my clan.
What was I supposed to do? Changing the technique so that it wouldn’t require an affinity would both weaken it and raise the amount of karmic energy needed to cultivate it.
In the end, I decided on a stop-gap solution. Eventually, I would need to improve the technique to fix this flaw, but until then, I could raise a single person’s affinity high enough that they could help everyone else.
After a brief conversation with ShouLi, we handed this job off to TongBin. He had proven his skills by being the first person to reach Peak Rank 5 in fire body cultivation, and he had been the one who had destroyed the first 3 rings of the formation beneath Dragon Gate. At the same time, his alchemy skills were rather weak, so he was having trouble gathering the contribution points needed to reach both Peak Emperor and Peak Rank 6 of body cultivation. So, letting him serve the clan by helping everyone master body cultivation was a win-win.
There was just one thing that I needed to do first.
“System, raise Su TongBin’s affinity for karmic energy to peak six-star. This only needs to be a ‘temporary’ boost that will last a single lifetime.”
Purchase confirmed. Cost 1,617,760,000 credits. 143,278,902,935 credits remaining.
As TongBin would stay in my inner world and not be reset by the time loops, a ‘temporary’ affinity was enough to last him the rest of his life, so I was able to save a few credits. I just had to hope that a peak six-star affinity would be enough for him to assist people with their Rank 4 techniques. While I still had enough credits to raise him to a high five-star, that would be expensive, so I didn’t want to do it if I didn’t have to.
After making this purchase, I spent some time teaching TongBin how to manipulate karmic energy in someone else’s body. Then, I sent him to Elder TaiZu to give him someone to practice on.
With this taken care of, I could finally shift my focus elsewhere.
At the start of this life, my inner world had only absorbed 34% of the Laws contained within the seed of the Solid Mountain Fire. While I wanted to get back to expanding the world, I had chosen to leave the Solid Mountain Fire in place since it was my world’s only source of both qi and Laws.
Now, over a hundred years later, neither of these was much of a concern. Most of the people had already left for the Wastes, and, more recently, the world had completed its absorption of the Solid Mountain Fire’s Laws.
Stolen from its rightful place, this narrative is not meant to be on Amazon; report any sightings.
Solid Mountain Fire, Profound-Rank, Elements: Earth, Consumes: Energy, Produces: Earth Qi, Laws Absorbed: 100%
Even after reaching 100%, the number of techniques that people could use in the world was limited, but that was good. I had wanted to enhance my analysis ability so that it would give me a detailed breakdown of exactly which Laws each seed possessed, but this wasn’t something that I could buy with credits, and after several attempts, I hadn’t been able to find any way to get such information from the System. However, these limitations on which cultivation techniques people could use provided me with a way to learn at least some of what I wanted to know
without
the System’s assistance.
I brought together a large group of Disciples, Masters, and Grandmasters and had them run through all my Warrior Tier earth qi techniques to make a list of which worked and which didn’t.
Nearly all the Yellow-Rank techniques in my library were usable. Even in Rank 3, there were only a handful that no one was able to cultivate, and the mental effects of those were all related to ideas like calmness, harmony, and sympathy.
For the Profound-Rank techniques, there was still a rather large variety that worked in Ranks 1 and 2. But in Rank 3, the only functional techniques were those relating to strength, resilience, and stubbornness.
No one was able to cultivate
any
of the Earth-Rank techniques.
How could I use this information? What did it tell me? I wasn’t sure.
One possibility was that Laws were structured like pyramids, where high-level Profound Laws were rooted in an ever-expanding collection of simpler Laws. Maybe the Solid Mountain Fire contained so many Yellow-Rank Laws because those were the necessary precursors to its Profound-Rank Laws.
If so, then this might mean that I shouldn’t worry too much about people cultivating a mess of low-level techniques. Doing so would help lay a foundation for learning more complex techniques later on.
However, another possibility was that fire seeds were simply… messy. Maybe the Yellow-Rank Laws weren’t there because they had to be. Maybe they were there because whoever—or whatever—created the seed didn’t know what they were doing.
In the end, all I could do was pass this information off to our trainers to see if they could find a way to make use of it while I moved on to the next task I needed to accomplish.
After sending a message to ShouLi to let her know what I was up to, I looked into my soul, shut down the Qi Gathering Formation, extracted the seed of the Solid Mountain Fire, and stored it away in a jade box.Thɪs updatᴇd by
Then, I flipped through my personal collection of fire seeds while also considering some of the seeds that others had picked up during their time in the Nine Rivers Sect. While a few of the Profound-Rank seeds did contain Laws of Earth, they were all multi-element seeds. The only single-element Profound Rank seed in my collection that contained Laws of Earth was the Solid Mountain Fire.
I didn’t see much value in spending time on Yellow-Rank seeds when I had other things that I needed to do, and I definitely didn’t want to start absorbing the Laws of a second element until after the world had reached its maximum size. So, I decided that it was finally time to stop working on Laws and start working on expansion.
I pulled out the seed of the Expanding Realms Fire and slotted it into my soul.
Over the past several decades, I had spent a lot of time thinking about exactly how I wanted to grow my inner world. One option was to simply continue its expansion outward, creating an endless, flat disc, but that seemed… boring.
With the freedom to mold my world into any shape that I could think of, why limit myself to a single flat disc? Why not create something a bit more unique?
After playing around with a few ideas, I finally came up with a plan that I was rather excited about. A while back, Bao had suggested that I should design my world around the Bagua Formation. Why not do something like that? Why not go further?
At the moment, my world had an area of 2 square kilometers. The first step in my plan was to increase that to roughly 6.5 square kilometers.
I did not plan to introduce any new elements directly into this space, however. It would remain a realm of earth, the ideal refuge for earth cultivators who were looking to enter seclusion. At the same time, it would also serve as a place where I could study the Laws of Earth in relative isolation.
After the expansion of this first disc was complete, I would then make two more.
There were three elements that touched earth on the Nine River’s Bagua diagram: fire, dark, and wood. Each of these had potential upsides, and I had yet to commit to which one I would use as my second element. I was leaning toward wood as that was in the center of the diagram and would open up more possibilities for the future, but fire, having a constructive relationship with earth, was also appealing.
In any case, no matter which one I ended up choosing, I planned to make a total of three equally sized discs. The first would remain focused on earth, the second would focus on my second element, and the third would be a place where these two elements could mingle and interact.
I wanted these three discs to, essentially, be three separate worlds. As the rules that governed my storage space dictated that these worlds would need to be connected to each other via tunnels, there were a few limitations that I would need to work around, but that was fine. Such tunnels would give people a way to traverse the different biomes without my assistance. I considered them to be more of a positive than a negative.
At any rate, this was a matter for the future. Before I could even
think
about constructing tunnels and secondary discs, I first had to more than triple the size of my existing disc. So, focusing on the task at hand, I wrapped the Expanding Realms Fire around my inner world and activated the Qi Gathering Formation.
Slowly, the edge of my inner world began to separate from the outer walls of Chang’an.
Expanding my inner world would take time, and there wasn’t anything that I could do to make it go any faster. So, once the expansion was underway, I pulled out the Drill of Fellowship and began cultivating.
With the number of cities we had at this point, we had an abundance of Lord-level karma, and I had access to as much of it as I required. So, I was able to advance all the way to the Peak of Rank 4 in less than a year.
After that, I turned my attention to Rank 5.

chapters.title: Chapter 314 – Life 76, Age 156, Martial Emperor Peak
chapters.content:
As the Rank 4 Drill of Fellowship had not been ‘novel’ enough to trigger an enlightenment, I had to struggle through the process of upgrading ShouLi’s Rank 5 and 6 techniques all on my own. However, the techniques that I was trying to create weren’t too different from the Rank 4 technique that I had already created. I mainly just needed to change where the blend of wu and karmic energy was applied.
This wasn’t overly difficult, and it only took me another few years to create these two new techniques.
Once they were complete, I began siphoning off a sizable portion of the karmic energy that was being generated from the members of the Su Clan. By infusing this energy into my nervous system, I was able to break through to Rank 5 in body cultivation, and by applying it to my viscera, I was able to break through to Rank 6.
In only a little over a decade, I was able to advance all the way from the Peak of Rank 4 to the Peak of Rank 6.
At this point, I no longer had a clear understanding of exactly what I had been doing to my body. For example, with each Rank of body cultivation, I had been circulating ever more powerful energy through my skin. At first, this had done little more than cause my tanned skin to turn somewhat pale. After Rank 4, my skin took on a faintly metallic hue. Now, at Rank 6, my entire body looked like it was made from frosted silver. Even my dark black hair had turned a silvery white.
Looking at my reflection in a mirror, I couldn’t help but feel that I had lost a part of my humanity.
But… did that really matter? After my death, I would be sent back to the start, and all of these changes would be wiped away. This body gave me the power that I would need if I wanted to rise to Sovereign, and, possibly, beyond.
Wondering exactly how powerful I had become, I took out my Rank 6 crescent moon spade and tapped the side of its shovel against my arm. The resulting sound was a bit muffled, but it carried the distinct ring of metal striking metal.
When I drew the blade of the shovel lightly across my forearm, the only result was a high-pitched scraping sound.
Wondering how much punishment my body could take, I pressed down and drew my shovel’s blade across my forearm once more.
Even with all the enhancements I had made to my muscles, it took a full tenth of my strength for a Rank 6 refined weapon to even break my skin. If I were up against a normal person with such a weapon, would they even be able to hurt me?Follow current novᴇls on novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
Of course, while I might not need to worry about attacks from bladed weapons, I wasn’t invincible. I had infused my body with metal energy to the point that I was now partially made of metal. This improved my defense against metal weapons, but metal was weak to fire. If I faced off against a powerful fire cultivator, or someone with a fire-based refined weapon, I would need to be extremely careful.
Still, since I would have needed to be extremely careful when fighting fire cultivators even before cultivating my body, this wasn’t exactly a downside. It was just something that I would need to keep in mind.
Wanting to perform more tests to find the limits of my new form, I stood and left the Hall of Ancestral Worship for the first time in several years.
If I wanted to accurately gauge my current combat power, I would need a sparring partner of equal strength, and I knew of two young men who would be able to fill that role perfectly. So, I headed directly to the Palace of Supreme Harmony to find them.
Unfortunately, when I arrived, the place was empty.
After checking around, I learned that the entire leadership council had left earlier in the day to visit the Grain Jar Sect. Having never heard of such a sect before, it took me a few moments to realize that this was the sect that Mei had set up in the southwestern corner of the Wastes—the sect for gu keepers.
Wondering both about the name and about why the entire leadership council had decided to pay it a visit, I immediately headed out to investigate.
As I left the Su Clan’s palace complex and walked through the streets of Dragon Gate, nearly everyone I passed stopped what they were doing to stare at me. Not wanting to be interrogated by inquisitive townsfolk, I used a movement technique to speed through the town too fast for anyone to notice me.
As movement techniques went, the one I used was rather basic. It was a simple Yellow-Rank technique that created a blade of metal qi to cut through the air in front of me. This didn’t improve my speed directly, but it allowed me to run as fast as I could without having to worry about creating a powerful wake in my passing.
As I ran through the city and picked my way through crowded streets, I was only able to reach a speed of around 50 kilometers per hour. However, once outside the city, I was able to more than double that. When I set myself and tried running as fast as I possibly could, I reached a speed of nearly 600 kilometers per hour.
This tale has been unlawfully lifted without the author's consent. Report any appearances on Amazon.
Overall, this was slightly disappointing. A Rank 5 wind horse would easily be able to outrun me. However, considering that they were bred for speed above all else, this wasn’t too surprising.
Running all out like this, it didn’t take me long to reach the border between the Dragon Gate Kingdom and the Grain Jar Sect.
As only the formation under Dragon Gate had its third ring destroyed, none of our Emperors were able to pass beyond the borders of the Dragon Gate Kingdom. So, when the leadership council had left to ‘visit the Grain Jar Sect,’ they had only been able to go as far as this border region where a small city of tents had been erected.
Upon seeing these tents, I broke from my full sprint and strolled forward at a much more leisurely pace.
Taking this time to look around at my surroundings, I noticed something… odd.
Usually, farmers in the Wastes would focus on growing medicinal herbs. Yes, food was important, but the money that a person could make from growing foodstuffs paled in comparison to what they could earn from growing blue peonies. GuiMing had even built large, multi-story greenhouses that focused on food production so that the more valuable open fields could be used for producing precious herbs.
So… why were all of the fields around me growing sorghum?
Stranger still, these fields had been outfitted with Qi Gathering Formations. Sorghum was a mortal food crop. It was capable of absorbing small quantities of qi, but it was entirely incapable of converting that qi into medicinal energy. Even if absorbed directly, the qi in sorghum didn’t
do
anything, so what was the point?
Looking back toward Dragon Gate City, I saw what I expected—fields of herbs. But looking toward the Grain Jar Sect, all I saw were fields of sorghum, wheat, barley, rice, and other grains. Was this why the leadership council had come here? Had this ‘Grain Jar Sect’ forced people to stop growing herbs? Why would they do that?
Confused, I continued forward to find out.
As I approached the tents, a pair of guards stepped forward to stop me. Upon seeing my strange, metallic complexion, they both narrowed their eyes and placed a hand on the hilts of their swords.
The guard on the left addressed me in a neutral tone. “Sorry, sir. No one is allowed to approach.”
I nodded to him amiably. “I understand. I am here to see ShouLi. Please tell her that Su Fang has arrived.”
The guard on the right growled. “Who do you think you are? How dare you call the Empress by her name?”
Both men were becoming visibly agitated. They were only seconds away from drawing their weapons to attack me.
I wasn’t sure what to do. I didn’t want to hurt ShouLi’s guards, but I also didn’t want to waste more time here than necessary. The problem was, I didn’t know the protocols for this kind of situation.
Without any better idea, I pulled out a gold coin and showed it to the men.
The guard on the right snarled. “Are you trying to bribe—”
I tossed the coin at him, and when it was halfway to him, I activated my will-lock to freeze it in place.
I looked at the guard on the left. “Please, go tell your superiors that Su Fang is here to speak with ShouLi.”
Thankfully, this guard was a bit smarter than his companion. He immediately ran off into the mess of tents.
The remaining guard and I were left to stare at each other in silence for a few minutes, but this tense atmosphere was soon broken by the noise of heavy footsteps.
Dozens of cultivators poured out of the small tent city, but I fixed my gaze on the person leading them: ShouLi.
When she saw me, she froze, and her eyes narrowed into slits. “Who are you?”
I smiled and opened my arms wide. “You… don’t recognize me? Has it really been that long?”
She blinked. “An… Ancestor? What… happened to you?”
With TongBin having taken over the distribution of our clan’s karmic energy, I no longer needed to visit ShouLi on a yearly basis. So, we hadn’t seen each other since shortly after I had advanced to Rank 4 of body cultivation. I knew that I looked different, but this reaction still seemed like a bit much.
I motioned toward the tents. “Let’s talk inside.”
She nodded slowly then guided me through the crowd and into a large tent pavilion.
Inside, there were several tables arranged in a horseshoe pattern. Each of these tables contained plates that were overflowing with various grains. Next to each plate, there was a large ceramic jug.
I looked around, confused. “What’s… going on here?”
ShouLi smirked. “Well, we
were
in the middle of discussing Sect Master LiMei’s new products.”
I raised an eyebrow, but ShouLi just gestured toward the jug sitting next to a plate of sorghum.
Upon picking it up and removing the lid, I was punched in the face with the odor of an extremely potent liquor. “What…”
Seeing my reaction, ShouLi coughed to keep from laughing. “The others are new, but that one… That one is the Grain Jar Sect’s original offering. Rank 2 baijiu. It’s cheap enough that a wealthy mortal can afford it while being potent enough to improve the cultivation base of even a Grandmaster.”
I turned on energy vision and looked into the jar.
At first, I just stared wide-eyed at the liquid that had been infused with a low level of extremely pure earth qi. However, my eyes were soon drawn to a faint ball of wind qi at its bottom.
“What is that?”
ShouLi didn’t answer my question. She just looked at the entrance of the pavilion.
Mei stepped inside and walked to a table on the opposite side of the horseshoe.
Then, she opened a jar and used a tendril of wind qi to pull out the object hidden inside.
It was a small worm.
She presented it to me. “This is a Rank 2 Liquor Gu. It feeds on various grains and converts them to alcohol. While we can grow them to Rank 3—and have even experimented with growing them to Rank 4—each worm can only produce a single pot of alcohol, so going beyond Rank 2 isn’t economical.”
Mei pointed to the various jars around the room. “Until now, we have mostly been using sorghum to produce baijiu. However, we are looking to expand our offerings to include whiskeys, vodkas, and gins.”
ShouLi cleared her throat. “The Grain Jar Sect’s baijiu is our most popular export. There is a high demand for it from people all over the continent, and we are the only ones producing it.”
I nodded slowly. “I… see. Keep up the good work.”
When I had given Mei the job of setting up a sect for gu keepers, I hadn’t known exactly what to expect, but I
definitely
hadn’t been expecting her to set up a distillery. This was… good… though, right?
I shook my head and refocused on ShouLi. While learning about what my new gu keeping sect was getting up to was nice, it wasn’t why I had come here.
“Where is everyone else? I need to have a little… talk… with Liang and NiangBa.”

chapters.title: Chapter 315 – Life 76, Age 156, Martial Emperor Peak
chapters.content:
ShouLi guided me out of the tent city and north, to a large, open field that had recently been sown with sorghum.
Seeing the tender young shoots that were just starting to poke up out of the soil, I felt a little bad about what we were planning to do. It was unlikely that any of them would be able to survive. Maybe it would be best to move them somewhere safe to protect them from the chaos that was about to unfold. Maybe…
